decisions.decision: Mount mode value encoding in explorer dropdown
decisions.choice: `<option value="mount:{uuid}">` with server-side prefix parsing
decisions.rationale: Single `<select>` value carries both mode type and mount identity. Avoids hidden inputs or second query param. Parser strips `mount:` prefix to extract UUID.

decisions.decision: Mount handler as prefix match, not EXPLORER_MODES entry
decisions.choice: `explorer_tree` checks `mode.startswith("mount:")` before registry lookup
decisions.rationale: Avoids polluting the static EXPLORER_MODES dict with per-mount entries. Single handler function handles all mounts via mount_id dispatch.

decisions.decision: Dynamic mount dropdown injection timing
decisions.choice: Fetch mounts after `initExplorerMode()`, then re-run mode restore for `mount:` prefixed stored modes
decisions.rationale: Avoids blocking initial page load. Built-in modes work immediately; mount options appear asynchronously. Re-check handles the case where stored mode is a mount that wasn't in the DOM during first restore.

decisions.decision: Separate mount-children endpoint from explorer/children
decisions.choice: New `GET /browser/explorer/mount-children?mount_id={id}&folder={folder}`
decisions.rationale: Mount folder expansion dispatches by VFS strategy (5 strategies × multiple depth levels), fundamentally different from hierarchy `dcterms:isPartOf` queries. Separate endpoint keeps dispatch clean.

decisions.decision: Tag property detection heuristic
decisions.choice: `'tags' in iri` or `'keywords' in iri` substring match
decisions.rationale: Only `bpkm:tags` and `schema:keywords` exist as tag properties. Simple substring match is sufficient and consistent across templates, save path, and SPARQL queries.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add explicit IRI set if more properties appear

decisions.decision: Multi-property by-tag SPARQL uses UNION, not VFS reuse
decisions.choice: Custom SPARQL with UNION across `bpkm:tags` and `schema:keywords` instead of reusing VFS `query_tag_folders`
decisions.rationale: VFS functions take single `tag_property` and `scope_filter` params — explorer needs multi-property, unscoped queries. Adapting would be more complex than writing fresh queries following the same pattern.

decisions.decision: Tag migration as admin endpoint, not startup hook
decisions.choice: `POST /browser/admin/migrate-tags` requiring owner role
decisions.rationale: No existing SPARQL migration infrastructure. Explicit endpoint avoids running migration on every startup. Idempotent — safe to call multiple times.
decisions.revisable: Yes — move to startup migration runner if one is built

decisions.decision: Tag-children as separate endpoint from tree_children and explorer/children
decisions.choice: `GET /browser/explorer/tag-children?tag={value}`
decisions.rationale: Tag queries use UNION across two properties with string-match FILTER, fundamentally different from type-based tree_children or isPartOf-based explorer/children. Follows D036/D040 pattern of separate endpoints per query shape.

decisions.decision: Favorites router as separate browser sub-module
decisions.choice: `backend/app/browser/favorites.py` with `favorites_router` included in `browser/router.py`
decisions.rationale: Follows D014 sub-router pattern. Favorites has its own endpoints (toggle, list) separate from workspace routes. Keeps workspace.py from growing further.

decisions.decision: FAVORITES section position in explorer pane
decisions.choice: Above OBJECTS section, not below
decisions.rationale: Favorites are high-traffic shortcuts — placing them above the main object list gives immediate visibility. Follows UX convention for quick-access sections.
decisions.revisable: Yes — move below if user feedback prefers

decisions.decision: Star icon toggle strategy
decisions.choice: Two `<i>` elements (outline + filled) with visibility toggle, not Lucide re-render
decisions.rationale: Avoids Lucide `createIcons()` re-render timing issues. Simpler DOM manipulation — toggle a class to swap which icon is visible.

decisions.decision: FAVORITES refresh via htmx trigger event
decisions.choice: `HX-Trigger: favoritesRefreshed` on toggle response + `hx-trigger="load, favoritesRefreshed from:body"` on section
decisions.rationale: htmx-native pattern for cross-component refresh. Toggle endpoint sets header; since star uses fetch (not htmx), JS dispatches `htmx.trigger(document.body, 'favoritesRefreshed')` after successful toggle.

decisions.decision: Comment soft-delete strategy
decisions.choice: Replace body with "[deleted]" and remove author triple, preserve comment IRI and replyTo structure
decisions.rationale: Avoids orphaned reply chains. Thread structure stays intact for readers. Simpler than cascade delete or tombstone patterns.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add hard-delete if storage becomes a concern

decisions.decision: Comment thread query strategy
decisions.choice: Flat SPARQL SELECT + Python tree assembly, not recursive SPARQL
decisions.rationale: RDF4J property paths can't carry metadata (author, timestamp) along the path. Flat query is simple, fast, and lets Python build the tree with full control over ordering and depth capping.

decisions.decision: Comments router as separate browser sub-module
decisions.choice: `backend/app/browser/comments.py` with `comments_router` included in `browser/router.py`
decisions.rationale: Follows D014/D045 sub-router pattern. Comments have their own CRUD endpoints separate from workspace routes.

decisions.decision: Comments router include order
decisions.choice: `comments_router` included before `objects_router` in `browser/router.py`
decisions.rationale: FastAPI's `:path` parameter in `objects_router` (`/object/{iri:path}`) is greedy and consumes `/comments` suffix, preventing comments endpoints from matching. Must register more-specific routes first.

decisions.decision: Ontology service as separate module
decisions.choice: `backend/app/ontology/` module (service.py + router.py), not added to existing services/
decisions.rationale: Ontology loading + TBox/ABox/RBox queries are a distinct domain boundary with startup responsibilities. Separate module keeps workspace.py from growing further and follows the domain-module pattern (canvas/, lint/, vfs/).

decisions.decision: Gist loading via batched INSERT DATA, not RDF4J REST upload
decisions.choice: Parse gist with rdflib → batch INSERT DATA (≤500 triples) via existing TriplestoreClient
decisions.rationale: Avoids adding a new RDF4J REST API method to TriplestoreClient. Batch size of 500 stays well under RDF4J's 2MB request body limit. Transaction-scoped for atomicity. Trade-off: slightly slower than direct Turtle upload but simpler and uses proven patterns.
decisions.revisable: Yes — switch to RDF4J REST graph upload if batch loading is too slow

decisions.decision: Ontology viewer as three-tab htmx layout in special-panel
decisions.choice: TBox/ABox/RBox as htmx-driven tabs inside a single `ontology_page.html`, TBox loads on open, ABox/RBox lazy-load on tab click
decisions.rationale: Simpler than dockview sub-panels. Consistent with how other workspace tabs work (canvas, VFS browser). htmx tab switching avoids JS complexity.

decisions.decision: TBox label resolution inline via SPARQL COALESCE, not LabelService batch
decisions.choice: TBox SPARQL uses `COALESCE(?skosLabel, ?rdfsLabel, localname)` directly in query
decisions.rationale: Gist uses `skos:prefLabel`, model classes use `rdfs:label`. Resolving in-query avoids a second round-trip to LabelService. LabelService.resolve_batch() is still used for ABox instances.
decisions.revisable: Yes — switch to LabelService if label resolution needs caching

decisions.decision: ABox shows only types with instances > 0
decisions.choice: Filter out classes with zero instances from ABox browser display
decisions.rationale: Gist has ~96 classes; most have zero instances in a typical SemPKM database. Showing all would overwhelm. D024 says gist is "fully visible" in TBox — ABox filtering by instance count is about data presence, not schema visibility.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add "show all types" toggle if users request

decisions.decision: Ontology router included in browser router coordinator
decisions.choice: `ontology_router` included before `objects_router` in `browser/router.py`
decisions.rationale: Same reason as D052: objects_router's `:path` parameter is greedy. Ontology routes use `/ontology/` prefix which would be consumed.

decisions.decision: User class IRI minting with UUID suffix
decisions.choice: `urn:sempkm:user-types:{Slug}-{uuid4hex[:8]}` (e.g. `urn:sempkm:user-types:MyTask-a1b2c3d4`)
decisions.rationale: Prevents IRI collision when multiple users create classes with the same name. Slug provides readability; UUID provides uniqueness. 8-hex-char prefix gives ~4 billion combinations — sufficient for user-created types.

decisions.decision: No EventStore for class/shape creation
decisions.choice: Direct INSERT DATA to `urn:sempkm:user-types`, same pattern as gist loading
decisions.rationale: Class creation is schema modification, not data modification. EventStore is for object-level operations. Consistent with how gist and ontology triples are loaded (D054).
decisions.revisable: Yes — add EventStore if class version history becomes a requirement

decisions.decision: IconService user-type icon resolution via triplestore triples
decisions.choice: Store `sempkm:typeIcon` and `sempkm:typeColor` triples on class IRI in `urn:sempkm:user-types`, with lazy-load cache on IconService
decisions.rationale: IconService is filesystem-only (manifest.yaml). User types have no filesystem manifest. Storing icon metadata as RDF triples is consistent with the RDF-first architecture and avoids introducing a separate JSON/YAML file for user types.
decisions.revisable: Yes — refactor if icon loading becomes a performance bottleneck

decisions.decision: Class deletion as DELETE WHERE, create-only scope expanded to include delete
decisions.choice: Minimum error recovery: `DELETE WHERE` removes class + shape triples from `urn:sempkm:user-types`
decisions.rationale: D028 scopes S08 as create-only, but without delete there's no recovery from broken classes. Delete is a single SPARQL operation, low effort, high value. Does not include edit (TYPE-03 scope).

decisions.decision: htmx form data serialization: use config-request not before-request
decisions.choice: `hx-on::config-request` with explicit `event.detail.parameters` update for dynamic form fields
decisions.rationale: htmx seals form parameters before `htmx:beforeRequest` fires. Hidden input values updated by JS during `beforeRequest` are not included in the request. `configRequest` fires during parameter collection phase, allowing explicit parameter injection.

decisions.decision: Shape delete uses two separate SPARQL UPDATE calls
decisions.choice: `_build_delete_shape_sparql()` returns tuple of (bnode cleanup, shape removal) queries
decisions.rationale: RDF4J rejects `OPTIONAL` inside `DELETE WHERE` (returns 400). Semicolon-separated updates in a single call also fail. Two sequential calls are reliable and equivalent.

decisions.decision: Chart.js 4.x via CDN, per-page only
decisions.choice: Chart.js 4.4 loaded via `{% block scripts %}` in model_detail.html only
decisions.rationale: Research recommendation. Battle-tested, ~60KB gzipped, supports sparkline + bar chart. No global loading — only admin model detail page needs it.
decisions.revisable: Yes — switch to bundled if build pipeline changes

decisions.decision: Lazy chart init on flip transitionend
decisions.choice: Charts created in flipCard() transitionend callback, not on page load
decisions.rationale: Chart.js reads canvas dimensions on init. Canvas inside `display:none` (face-hidden) has 0×0 dimensions → empty charts. Lazy init after flip ensures canvas is visible.

decisions.decision: Link distribution buckets: 0, 1-2, 3-5, 6-10, 11+
decisions.choice: Fixed 5-bucket histogram for link count distribution
decisions.rationale: Covers the typical power-law distribution of knowledge graph connectivity. Simple to compute in SPARQL with CASE/BIND. Readable in a small bar chart.
decisions.revisable: Yes — adjust buckets if real usage shows different distribution

decisions.decision: Growth trend window: 8 weeks
decisions.choice: Query last 8 weeks of object.create events with timestamp filter
decisions.rationale: Balances sparkline readability (8 data points) with query performance (tight time bound avoids full event scan).
decisions.revisable: Yes — extend if users want longer history

decisions.decision: Rate-limit e2e tests run last via 99- directory prefix
decisions.choice: Rate-limiting spec in `e2e/tests/99-rate-limiting/`
decisions.rationale: Rate-limit tests exhaust the per-IP endpoint budget (slowapi in-memory), breaking auth fixtures in subsequent tests. Moving to 99- ensures Playwright's alphabetical ordering runs them after all auth-dependent tests.

decisions.decision: Two-step class delete confirmation via check endpoint
decisions.choice: `GET /ontology/delete-class-check` returns HTML fragment with instance/subclass counts, rendered in modal overlay. Confirm button triggers existing `DELETE /ontology/delete-class`.
decisions.rationale: `hx-confirm` uses browser-native `window.confirm()` which cannot show dynamic content. Two-step pattern follows existing modal conventions (class creation, property creation, class edit).

decisions.decision: `_property_source` returns `'user'` for user-types IRIs
decisions.choice: Check for `urn:sempkm:user-types:` prefix before generic `SEMPKM_NS` check
decisions.rationale: Fixes RBox badge showing "sempkm" instead of "user" for user-created properties. IRI prefix ordering matters since user-types IRIs also start with `urn:sempkm:`.

decisions.decision: Property deletion: simple `hx-confirm`, no modal
decisions.choice: Properties have no instances and no dependent shapes to warn about. Static `hx-confirm` string is sufficient.
decisions.rationale: Avoids over-engineering. Class deletion needs dynamic counts; property deletion doesn't.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add modal if property deletion gains cascade concerns

decisions.decision: Property type immutable on edit
decisions.choice: Edit form shows property type (Object/Datatype) as read-only; cannot switch after creation
decisions.rationale: Switching between ObjectProperty and DatatypeProperty changes IRI semantics and breaks SHACL shapes that reference the property. Safer to require delete + re-create.

decisions.decision: Custom section server-rendered in admin_models(), not htmx lazy-load
decisions.choice: Extend `admin_models()` to call `list_user_types()` and pass result to template
decisions.rationale: The `list_user_types()` query hits a single small graph (<100ms). Lazy-load adds unnecessary complexity.
decisions.revisable: Yes — switch to htmx lazy-load if query becomes slow

decisions.decision: SHACL shapes NOT updated on property edit
decisions.choice: When domain/range changes, existing SHACL shapes referencing the property are not auto-updated
decisions.rationale: SHACL shapes reference properties by IRI via `sh:path`. Domain/range are OWL-level constraints, not SHACL-level. Acceptable because shapes still point to the correct IRI.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add shape cascade if it causes user confusion

decisions.decision: Edit property form uses `epf-` ID prefix
decisions.choice: Edit property form element IDs prefixed `epf-` to avoid collision with create form `cpf-` IDs
decisions.rationale: Both forms can coexist in the DOM (ontology page has both modals). ID collision would break JS handlers.

decisions.decision: Pre-commit hook rejects conflict markers
decisions.choice: `.githooks/pre-commit` scans staged files for `^<<<<<<< ` / `^=======` / `^>>>>>>> ` and exits non-zero if found
decisions.rationale: 17 consecutive squash merges (M002/S03–M005/S01) committed conflict markers to main undetected. Docker volume mounts hid the damage by serving clean branch code. Pre-commit hook is the last line of defense.

decisions.decision: Migrations volume-mounted in docker-compose.yml
decisions.choice: `./backend/migrations:/app/migrations` added to api service volumes
decisions.rationale: Without this mount, migration file edits required a full `docker compose build api`. Consistent with how `./backend/app` is already mounted. Discovered when conflict-marker fix in `env.py` wasn't picked up by the running container.

decisions.decision: Ops log calls in router layer, not service layer
decisions.choice: `log_activity()` called from admin router, inference router, and validation queue — not from `ModelService`/`InferenceService`
decisions.rationale: Router layer already has user context from `require_role()`. Threading user IRIs through service methods would change signatures and create coupling. Consistent with how `EventStore.commit()` receives `performed_by` from routers.

decisions.decision: Ops log uses direct SPARQL INSERT DATA, not EventStore
decisions.choice: Direct SPARQL INSERT DATA to `urn:sempkm:ops-log` named graph
decisions.rationale: Ops log records metadata _about_ operations, not data belonging in `urn:sempkm:current`. Same pattern as `QueryService` writes to `urn:sempkm:queries`. EventStore would create per-event graphs and materialize into current — wrong semantics.

decisions.decision: Single `urn:sempkm:ops-log` named graph for all entries
decisions.choice: All ops log activities in one graph, not per-entry graphs
decisions.rationale: Matches `urn:sempkm:queries` pattern from S01. Log entries are simple metadata — no data isolation needed. Single graph simplifies querying. Low volume (10-50 entries/day max).

decisions.decision: Ops log calls are fire-and-forget with try/except
decisions.choice: All `log_activity()` calls wrapped in try/except — failures logged at WARNING but never block primary operation
decisions.rationale: Ops log is observability tooling. A triplestore write failure during model install must not prevent the install from succeeding. Same philosophy as webhook dispatch.

decisions.decision: htmx target-aware block rendering for ops log route
decisions.choice: Check `HX-Target` header to decide which Jinja2 block to return: `app-content` → `content` block (sidebar nav), anything else → `table_rows` block (filter/pagination)
decisions.rationale: Single endpoint serves three use cases (full page, sidebar nav, filter/pagination). Without target detection, returning `content` block for filter swaps caused duplicate heading/controls inside `#ops-log-table`.

decisions.decision: Hierarchical tag tree: fetch flat, nest in Python, lazy-load children
decisions.choice: Existing SPARQL fetches all tags flat; `build_tag_tree()` pure function groups into hierarchy; `tag_children` endpoint with `prefix` param for lazy sub-folder loading
decisions.rationale: Reuses existing SPARQL (no new string functions for roots), uses `STRSTARTS` for children (well-supported), pure function is unit-testable without Docker. Follows proven htmx lazy-load pattern (D035, D036, D040, D044).

decisions.decision: `tag_children` endpoint extended with `prefix` parameter, not new endpoint
decisions.choice: Add `prefix` query param to existing `GET /explorer/tag-children` rather than creating a separate `/explorer/tag-prefix-children` route
decisions.rationale: Existing endpoint already handles tag expansion. Prefix queries are the same domain — sub-folder expansion is conceptually "children of a tag prefix". `tag` param = exact match objects, `prefix` param = sub-folder tree. Avoids endpoint proliferation while staying clean.
decisions.revisable: Yes — split if logic diverges significantly

decisions.decision: `build_tag_tree()` as separate module, not inline in workspace.py
decisions.choice: New `backend/app/browser/tag_tree.py` module for pure function
decisions.rationale: workspace.py is already 1063 lines. Pure function has no dependencies on FastAPI/triplestore — separate module keeps it testable and workspace.py from growing.

decisions.decision: Tag autocomplete q parameter via htmx:configRequest, not hx-vals
decisions.choice: `htmx:configRequest` event listener rewrites params to `{q: triggerEl.value}` for tag-suggestions requests
decisions.rationale: `hx-vals='js:{"q": this.value}'` did not reliably pass the `q` query parameter on htmx GET requests — requests were sent without `q`, returning all tags unfiltered. `htmx:configRequest` fires during parameter collection and allows explicit injection.

decisions.decision: Refresh clears 4 artifact graphs inline, not via `clear_model_graphs()`
decisions.choice: Build 4 individual `CLEAR SILENT GRAPH` statements for ontology/shapes/views/rules, not reuse `clear_model_graphs()`
decisions.rationale: `clear_model_graphs()` clears all 5 graphs including seed. Refresh must NOT touch seed (user data). Adding an `exclude` parameter would change the function signature for one caller. Inline CLEAR is simpler and explicit.

decisions.decision: Refresh uses hx-confirm, not two-step modal
decisions.choice: Simple `hx-confirm` dialog on Refresh button
decisions.rationale: Refresh is non-destructive (transactional — rollback on failure). Lower risk than delete. Two-step modal (D070) is for operations with permanent data loss potential.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add modal if refresh gains destructive side effects

decisions.decision: PROV-O Starting Point terms only — no Qualified or Extended
decisions.choice: Use `prov:Activity`, `prov:startedAtTime`, `prov:wasAssociatedWith`, etc. Do not use `prov:qualifiedAssociation`, `prov:hadRole`, or Extended terms
decisions.rationale: Qualified terms add blank nodes and multi-triple patterns for marginal information gain. Starting Point covers 90%+ of SemPKM's provenance needs. Ops log already validates this approach.
decisions.revisable: Yes — reconsider if provenance queries need role-on-association detail

decisions.decision: Existing event graphs retain sempkm: predicates forever — no retroactive migration
decisions.choice: Immutable event named graphs keep their original `sempkm:` predicates. Alignment applies only to newly written data via dual-write.
decisions.rationale: Event-sourcing requires immutable events. Federation sync transmits events as serialized patches — changing predicates would desynchronize instances. Dual-write + COALESCE queries handle mixed-era data without rewriting history.

decisions.decision: COALESCE pattern for dual-predicate SPARQL queries (over UNION or VALUES)
decisions.choice: Use `OPTIONAL { ?e sempkm:timestamp ?old } OPTIONAL { ?e prov:startedAtTime ?new } BIND(COALESCE(?new, ?old) AS ?ts)`
decisions.rationale: VALUES creates cross-products on dual-write events. UNION requires deduplication. COALESCE with OPTIONAL is clean, single-row-per-event, and performs well on most triplestores.
decisions.revisable: Yes — revisit if triplestore performance shows issues with OPTIONAL chains

decisions.decision: Generic views registered in-memory at startup, not as RDF
decisions.choice: Register 3 generic ViewSpecs (Table/Cards/Graph) in ViewSpecService at startup, not in a system named graph
decisions.rationale: Avoids a "system views" named graph. Generic views are code-defined behavior, not data-defined. Simpler lifecycle — no migration needed for view definition changes.
decisions.revisable: Yes — move to RDF if user-customizable generic views become a requirement

decisions.decision: SHACL shapes via ShapesService as column discovery source
decisions.choice: Use ShapesService._extract_node_shape() → PropertyShape.path/name/order for dynamic table columns
decisions.rationale: Already extracts sh:path, sh:name, sh:order — everything needed for dynamic columns. Fallback to default column set (label, type, created, modified) for types with ≤2 properties.

decisions.decision: Type filter pills for cross-type generic views
decisions.choice: Pills (not dropdown, not carousel) for type selection in generic views
decisions.rationale: Carousel assumes single target_class. Dropdown hides available types. Pills show all types at a glance with active state. Consistent with tag pill UX pattern.
decisions.revisable: Yes — reconsider if type count exceeds ~15

decisions.decision: sempkm:scopeQuery for view-to-query scope binding
decisions.choice: Distinct from sempkm:fromQuery: scopeQuery = runtime filter, fromQuery = provenance
decisions.rationale: Extends existing promoted view pattern. scopeQuery injects VALUES clause or subquery to limit view results to query output IRIs. Clean separation of concerns.

decisions.decision: 3-phase views migration, additive-first
decisions.choice: Phase 1 (generic views alongside existing tree), Phase 2 (consolidate explorer), Phase 3 (cleanup). Phase 1 is milestone deliverable.
decisions.rationale: No big-bang. Phase 1 is strictly additive — zero risk to existing views. Phase 2 changes navigation only. Phase 3 is dead code removal.

decisions.decision: Direct SPARQL via SyncTriplestoreClient for VFS saved query resolution
decisions.choice: `SyncTriplestoreClient` queries `urn:sempkm:queries` graph directly, not async `QueryService`
decisions.rationale: WebDAV runs in sync WSGI context. `QueryService` is async (uses `httpx.AsyncClient`). Calling async from sync would require `asyncio.run()` or thread bridging — fragile in production. `SyncTriplestoreClient` already used by VFS provider code.

decisions.decision: VFS adopts `sempkm:scopeQuery` with full IRI (aligning with Views Rethink)
decisions.choice: Replace bare UUID `sempkm:savedQueryId` with `sempkm:scopeQuery` predicate pointing to full `urn:sempkm:query:{uuid}` IRI
decisions.rationale: Matches Views Rethink D096 pattern. Full IRI enables SPARQL joins without string manipulation. One predicate used by both views and VFS for scope binding. Migration: one SPARQL UPDATE renames predicate + wraps values.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if model query IRIs need different treatment

decisions.decision: Chain model (Option A) for composable VFS strategies, max depth 3
decisions.choice: Ordered list of strategies, each level nests inside the previous. Max 3 levels enforced.
decisions.rationale: Chain is simpler than tree or graph composition. 3 levels covers all practical use cases (e.g. by-tag → by-type → flat). Provider path dispatch needs extension from 4 to 6 segments.

decisions.decision: type_filter AND saved_query compose via AND
decisions.choice: Both `sempkm:typeFilter` VALUES clause and saved query scope filter applied simultaneously
decisions.rationale: AND semantics match user mental model: "show me Notes (type) from this query (scope)". OR would produce confusing results. Implementation: both clauses injected into the same WHERE block.

decisions.decision: Defer auto-refresh for VFS, use existing 30s TTLCache
decisions.choice: No file-system watcher or push invalidation. Rely on existing `TTLCache(maxsize=64, ttl=30)` in VFS provider.
decisions.rationale: Auto-refresh adds complexity (filesystem watchers, WebSocket push) for marginal benefit. 30s TTL means changes appear within half a minute. Revisit when write-support lands.

decisions.decision: Dashboard builder submits via fetch(), not htmx form
decisions.choice: Builder form uses `fetch()` with `Content-Type: application/json` to POST/PATCH the existing JSON API endpoints
decisions.rationale: JSON API expects structured `{name, layout, blocks}` body. htmx form submission sends form-encoded data which doesn't map cleanly to nested JSON. `fetch()` also allows JS-side payload construction from dynamic block rows. Same pattern as VFS mount form.

decisions.decision: Explorer refresh via JS-dispatched htmx trigger, not HX-Trigger header
decisions.choice: Builder's `fetch()` success handler calls `htmx.trigger(document.body, 'dashboardsRefreshed')`
decisions.rationale: JSON API endpoints return JSON, not HTML. `HX-Trigger` response header only works with htmx-initiated requests. Since builder uses `fetch()`, JS must dispatch the event manually. Follows D048 pattern (favorites).

decisions.decision: Single implicit IRI context variable per dashboard, not Retool-style named variables
decisions.choice: Dashboard has one context variable — the selected IRI. Source blocks export it, consumer blocks bind it to a named SPARQL variable via `listens_to_context`.
decisions.rationale: Simplest viable approach. Single IRI covers primary use case (select project → filter notes). Multiple named variables can layer on later without breaking the single-IRI API.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add named variables if dashboards need multiple independent filters

decisions.decision: htmx:configRequest for context_iri URL injection, not hx-vals
decisions.choice: Consumer blocks use `htmx:configRequest` event listener to inject `context_iri` and `context_var` params into re-fetch URLs
decisions.rationale: `hx-vals` with `js:` prefix is unreliable for dynamic values in this codebase (see D087). `htmx:configRequest` fires during parameter collection and allows explicit injection. Proven pattern from tag autocomplete.

decisions.decision: Context emission limited to table renderer for v1
decisions.choice: Only table rows emit `sempkm:dashboard-context-changed`. Cards (flip animation conflict) and graphs (Cytoscape events) deferred.
decisions.rationale: Table is the primary use case. Card clicks trigger flip, not selection. Graph node clicks need Cytoscape event listeners — separate concern. Both can be added later without changing the event contract.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add card/graph context emission when needed

decisions.decision: dashboard_mode query parameter for conditional row behavior
decisions.choice: `dashboard_mode=1` query param on view endpoints tells table_view template to emit context events instead of openTab()
decisions.rationale: Clean separation: same template renders correctly in both dashboard-embedded and standalone contexts. No global state or CSS class sniffing. Passed from render_block through the view URL.

decisions.decision: Dashboard context event uses camelCase, not colon-namespaced
decisions.choice: Event name `dashboardContextChanged` instead of `sempkm:dashboard-context-changed`
decisions.rationale: htmx's hx-trigger parser uses colons as modifier separators (like `from:body`). Custom event names containing colons fail to register as trigger listeners. camelCase matches existing codebase pattern (dashboardsRefreshed, favoritesRefreshed).

decisions.decision: Context params forwarded server-side in render_block, not purely client-side
decisions.choice: render_block accepts context_iri/context_var and embeds them in the view URL
decisions.rationale: htmx:configRequest on nested elements (inner view div inside slot div) causes duplicate parameter injection. Server-side forwarding gives clean, single-injection chain: configRequest on slot → render_block → view URL.

decisions.decision: Default SELECT query uses mandatory rdf:type binding
decisions.choice: `?s rdf:type ?type .` is non-OPTIONAL in `_build_default_select()`
decisions.rationale: All-OPTIONAL patterns left `?s` unbound — SPARQL engines return zero rows because there's no triple pattern to ground the subject variable. Making type mandatory ensures subjects have at least one typed assertion.

decisions.decision: Generic graph view uses separate data endpoint
decisions.choice: `GET /browser/views/generic/{renderer}/data` instead of retrofitting existing `/graph/{spec_iri}/data`
decisions.rationale: Generic specs have empty `sparql_query` — queries are built dynamically per request. The existing data endpoint calls `execute_graph_query(spec)` which returns empty when `spec.sparql_query` is empty. Separate endpoint keeps both paths clean.
decisions.revisable: Yes — could unify if generic specs stored built queries

decisions.decision: pagination_base_url template variable for URL construction
decisions.choice: All pagination/sort/filter templates accept `pagination_base_url \
decisions.rationale: default(old_pattern)`
decisions.revisable: Generic views use `?type=` query params instead of spec IRI path segments. The `\

decisions.decision: Generic view tabs use special-panel dockview component, not view-panel
decisions.choice: `openGenericViewTab()` creates a `special-panel` with `specialType: 'generic-view'` and `renderer` param
decisions.rationale: Generic views don't have a spec IRI — `view-panel`'s URL construction assumes `/{renderer}/{encoded_iri}` which doesn't fit. `special-panel` pattern already proven by canvas, ontology, dashboard, and workflow tabs.

decisions.decision: Saved Views replaces MY VIEWS as htmx lazy-loaded folder inside VIEWS section
decisions.choice: Saved Views folder in views_explorer.html uses `hx-trigger="intersect once"` loading from `/browser/my-views`
decisions.rationale: Removes a sidebar section. `/browser/my-views` endpoint stays unchanged. `#my-views-tree` → `#saved-views-tree` ID update in `my_views.html` and `sparql-console.js`.

decisions.decision: type_filter VALUES uses ?iri a ?type binding
decisions.choice: `VALUES ?type { ... }` with `?iri a ?type .` in scope filter
decisions.rationale: Connects the VALUES constraint to the object pattern via rdf:type triple. Empty list treated same as None (no-op).

decisions.decision: scope_query stores full IRI, not bare UUID
decisions.choice: `<urn:sempkm:query:{uuid}>` as RDF IRI type
decisions.rationale: Enables SPARQL joins without string manipulation. Frontend constructs IRI by prefixing `urn:sempkm:query:` to UUID. Aligns with D099.

decisions.decision: Two-query approach for list_mounts type_filter
decisions.choice: Separate SELECT for typeFilter triples, merged in Python
decisions.rationale: More portable across SPARQL 1.1 stores than GROUP_CONCAT subquery. GROUP_CONCAT used for single-resource queries (get_by_id, get_by_prefix) where it's safe.
decisions.revisable: Yes — consolidate if store supports GROUP_CONCAT reliably

decisions.decision: Preview returns HTTP 404 for unresolvable scope_query
decisions.choice: Fail-fast with clear error instead of empty scope
decisions.rationale: Dead code previously produced empty scope_filter regardless of input. 404 makes the failure visible to API callers. WebDAV path silently omits scope (warning logged) since crashing a directory listing is worse.

decisions.decision: Chain strategies stored as pipe-delimited string literal
decisions.choice: `"by-tag\
decisions.rationale: by-date"` stored as single string via `sempkm:directoryStrategy`
decisions.revisable: RDF doesn't have native ordered lists without blank nodes. Pipe-delimited string avoids sequence predicate complexity. Parsed via `strategy.split("\

decisions.decision: Chain scope narrowing is cumulative across all parent levels
decisions.choice: Each chain depth adds WHERE clauses for ALL parent groupings, not just the immediate parent
decisions.rationale: Objects at depth 2 must match both depth-0 and depth-1 groupings. Prevents leaked results from sibling branches. Narrowing filters composed as additional WHERE clause fragments via `build_chain_narrowing_filter()`.

decisions.decision: Filename template expansion before slugification
decisions.choice: Template variables expanded to raw text, then entire string slugified
decisions.rationale: Preserves filesystem safety. `{date}-{title}` → `"2024-01-15-My Note"` → `"2024-01-15-my-note"`. Dedup suffix applies after slugification as before.

decisions.decision: Chain by-type narrowing uses SPARQL local name FILTER, not pre-resolved IRI
decisions.choice: `FILTER(REPLACE(STR(?type), ".*[/:#]", "") = "Label")` instead of `?iri a <resolved-iri>`
decisions.rationale: `build_chain_narrowing_filter()` is a pure function without triplestore access. Resolving type label→IRI requires a SPARQL query (done in StrategyFolderCollection._resolve_type_iri_from_label). The FILTER approach works at query time and avoids coupling the narrowing helper to the sync client.
decisions.revisable: Yes — could pre-resolve if perf matters

decisions.decision: Dual-layer rendering for embed nodes
decisions.choice: Embed iframes in a separate persistent DOM layer; regular nodes in the innerHTML-rebuilt dynamic layer
decisions.rationale: `renderNodes()` rebuilds `state.layer.innerHTML` every drag frame. Iframes recreated via innerHTML lose their loaded page state. Dual-layer avoids this: embed nodes are created/moved via `style.left`/`style.top` updates, never innerHTML-rebuilt.

decisions.decision: Separate `base_embed.html` template for iframe content
decisions.choice: New minimal base template, not conditional hiding in `base.html`
decisions.rationale: `base.html` loads 15+ CDN scripts (Cytoscape, dockview, CodeMirror, etc.) and the sidebar. Embed pages need only htmx + theme CSS + content. Separate template avoids iframe payload bloat and fragility of hiding elements in a shared template.

decisions.decision: Property flip uses inline rendering, not iframes
decisions.choice: Compact label/value table built from JSON API response, rendered directly in the node DOM
decisions.rationale: SHACL-derived property data is lightweight (10-30 key/value pairs). Inline rendering is faster, lighter, and avoids iframe overhead for the most common flip action. Only views/dashboards/SPARQL/object-read use iframe embeds.

decisions.decision: CSS resize handles over native CSS `resize: both`
decisions.choice: Custom pointer-event resize handles on node corners/edges
decisions.rationale: CSS `resize: both` only provides a bottom-right handle, doesn't emit events for state persistence, and can't enforce min/max constraints. Custom handles provide better UX and integrate with the existing pointer event system.

decisions.decision: Max 8 simultaneous iframe embeds, hard limit
decisions.choice: Hard cap on embed count with user warning at placement time
decisions.rationale: Each iframe is a full page load. 5+ embeds measurably impacts performance. Hard limit for v1 prevents browser tab crashes. Lazy loading deferred to follow-up.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add lazy loading or raise limit if needed

decisions.decision: Embed link routing via `window.parent`
decisions.choice: Links inside embed iframes open targets in parent workspace via `window.parent.openTab()`
decisions.rationale: Same-origin iframes can access parent window. This routes clicks to dockview tabs in the main workspace instead of navigating the iframe away from embedded content.

decisions.decision: Resize updates inline style during drag, full renderNodes on pointerUp
decisions.choice: During resize: update `style.width`/`style.height` directly on the DOM element + update node model. On pointerUp: call `renderNodes()` once to finalize edges and DOM state.
decisions.rationale: `renderNodes()` rebuilds `state.layer.innerHTML` on every call. Calling it on every resize frame would be expensive and cause visual flicker (SVG edges rebuilt). Direct style manipulation during drag is smooth; final `renderNodes()` ensures edges re-calculate from final box dimensions.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if dual-layer rendering (S03) changes the rebuild model

decisions.decision: Property cache is memory-only, not serialized
decisions.choice: `state.propertyCache` keyed by nodeId, re-fetched on session load via `applyDocument()` triggering `fetchNodeProperties()` for nodes with `showProperties: true`
decisions.rationale: Serializing property data would bloat canvas session JSON and stale quickly. Re-fetching on load ensures fresh data. Follows the `fetchNodeBody` pattern where markdown is also re-fetched.

decisions.decision: `build_property_list()` extracted as pure function
decisions.choice: Core property-building logic in standalone function taking parsed bindings, form, and labels as input
decisions.rationale: Enables 26 unit tests with zero mocking — all inputs are plain dicts/lists. Endpoint handler orchestrates async calls then delegates to pure function. Pattern reusable for future canvas data transformations.

decisions.decision: New `GET /browser/sparql-result/{query_id}` endpoint for server-rendered query results
decisions.choice: Fetch saved query, execute via `_execute_sparql()`, render HTML table in `base_embed.html`
decisions.rationale: Existing SPARQL console renders results client-side (CodeMirror + custom JS). No server-rendered endpoint exists for saved query output. Embeds need an HTML page, not a JS-rendered SPA. Reuses existing query execution helpers.

decisions.decision: Embed layer uses `pointer-events: none` with `auto` on individual embeds
decisions.choice: Container `.spatial-canvas-embed-layer` has `pointer-events: none`; individual `.spatial-node-embed` elements have `pointer-events: auto`
decisions.rationale: Lets clicks pass through empty areas of the embed layer to reach regular nodes on the layer below. Without this, the embed layer's higher DOM position would intercept all pointer events over the canvas.

decisions.decision: Fragment-to-string rendering for embed wrapping
decisions.choice: `_embed_response()` calls `templates.env.get_template(name).render(context)` to get fragment HTML, passes it as `content` to `embed_wrapper.html`
decisions.rationale: Jinja2 `{% include inner_template %}` with a variable template name has scoping issues and requires the template name to be a string constant in some Jinja2 configurations. Rendering to string first is simpler, works with any fragment template, and the embed wrapper just needs `{{ content

decisions.decision: SPARQL result router registered as browser sub-module before objects_router
decisions.choice: `sparql_result_router` in `browser/router.py` mounted before `objects_router`
decisions.rationale: The objects_router has `{object_iri:path}` catch-all patterns that would consume `/sparql-result/*` URLs. Registration order in FastAPI determines route matching priority. Same pattern as ontology_router and comments_router.

decisions.decision: Dual-layer rendering: regular nodes via innerHTML, embeds via persistent DOM
decisions.choice: `state.layer` rebuilt via innerHTML each `renderNodes()` call; `state.embedLayer` only updates CSS position/size properties on existing DOM elements
decisions.rationale: iframes lose their loaded state when recreated via innerHTML. Persistent DOM for embeds means the iframe never gets destroyed during regular node interactions. Orphan cleanup runs each render to remove stale embed elements. Embed layer applies same CSS transform as regular layer for pan/zoom sync.

decisions.decision: Apps as sandboxed subprocesses, not in-process or Docker containers
decisions.choice: Each app runs in its own Python subprocess with its own venv, communicating via HTTP over unix domain socket
decisions.rationale: Subprocess gives dependency isolation and crash isolation without Docker-in-Docker complexity. HTTP/UDS is debuggable with standard tooling. In-process would allow apps to crash the platform; Docker containers add networking/orchestration overhead.
decisions.revisable: Yes — upgrade to containers if untrusted marketplace apps are added

decisions.decision: Mental models are always shared — apps never bundle their own model
decisions.choice: Models published independently, versioned on own timeline, reusable by any app. App declares model dependencies with semver ranges.
decisions.rationale: Composability: multiple apps can share the same model. Independent versioning prevents tight coupling. Data survives app removal.

decisions.decision: App data lives in urn:sempkm:current, not a separate graph
decisions.choice: Apps produce data through standard EventStore (including bulk mode). Data typed by shared models is first-class — browsable, queryable, linkable. IRI prefix for traceability/cleanup.
decisions.rationale: Separate graphs would fragment the knowledge graph. Shared graph means articles are as queryable as user-created notes. IRI prefix enables clean uninstall.

decisions.decision: Platform owns scheduling — apps declare tasks, platform runs them
decisions.choice: AppScheduler in main process triggers app tasks via HTTP. Admin has full visibility and control (pause, adjust interval, view history).
decisions.rationale: Centralized control prevents rogue apps from overwhelming the system. Admin can pause all tasks. Consistent monitoring surface.

decisions.decision: All app UI is fragments — platform controls the page shell
decisions.choice: Apps return HTML fragments loaded via htmx. Platform renders sidebar, header, theming. Apps cannot break platform navigation.
decisions.rationale: Consistent UX, theme compliance, no iframe overhead. Apps can't hijack navigation or break workspace layout.

decisions.decision: App SDK as in-repo package, not published to PyPI
decisions.choice: SDK lives at backend/sdk/ in the SemPKM repo. Installed into app venvs at install time.
decisions.rationale: Simpler development loop. SDK and platform evolve together. No package publishing infrastructure needed for v1.
decisions.revisable: Yes — publish to PyPI when marketplace launches

decisions.decision: browserVisible field on Mental Model types (default true)
decisions.choice: Types with `browserVisible: false` are hidden from object browser but remain queryable via SPARQL and linkable via edges.
decisions.rationale: Apps create internal bookkeeping types (ReadActivity, sync cursors) that clutter the object browser. Hiding them improves UX without losing data access. Backward compatible (default true).

decisions.decision: Bulk EventStore with summary metadata, not per-operation
decisions.choice: `commit_bulk()` records ~10 triples per batch vs. ~5N for standard. All-or-nothing undo.
decisions.rationale: Feed polling creates 50-150 operations per update. Per-operation metadata overhead is unacceptable. Bulk undo semantics are fine for batch ingestion.

decisions.decision: First-party apps in apps/ directory alongside models/
decisions.choice: Apps committed to repo. Platform discovers them at startup. Consistent with models/ pattern for Mental Models.
decisions.rationale: Simple installation for bundled apps. No marketplace infrastructure needed for v1.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add marketplace when app ecosystem grows

decisions.decision: Right pane sections dynamic vs. hardcoded
decisions.choice: Single dynamic endpoint merging platform sections + app contributions, replacing 3 hardcoded <details> blocks
decisions.rationale: App contributions need to appear alongside Relations/Lint/Comments. Dynamic endpoint allows runtime merging based on object type and running apps. AbortController cancellation prevents stale sections on rapid tab switching. Platform sections always present as baseline; app sections gracefully degraded on failure.

decisions.decision: Object renderer override dispatch pattern
decisions.choice: Registry checks type match → pref table overrides → template swap with context augmentation; failure falls back silently to default SHACL form
decisions.rationale: Apps need to replace default SHACL form for specific types with custom read/edit renderers. Three-layer dispatch (registry → pref → template) gives clear precedence. AppRendererPref table resolves multi-app conflicts via admin UI. Silent fallback to default on any error ensures renderer bugs never break object viewing.

decisions.decision: M011 is pure content — no platform code changes
decisions.choice: All 4 models shipped as .sempkm-model archives using existing manifest/loader/validator/inference/validation pipeline. Zero Python, JS, or CSS changes.
decisions.rationale: Research confirmed every pattern needed (SPARQLConstraint, PropertyGroups, editHelpText, inverseOf, SavedQuery) is already exercised by basic-pkm and PPV. Adding platform features would increase risk for no benefit.

decisions.decision: Dashboard bundling deferred — document recommended configs
decisions.choice: Dashboards described in design doc cannot be shipped in model archives (DashboardSpec is SQLite JSON per D105). Document recommended dashboard configurations in user guide instead.
decisions.rationale: DashboardSpec-to-RDF migration is tracked tech debt. Adding manifest dashboard support is a platform change that violates M011's pure-content scope.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add dashboard manifest support when DashboardSpec moves to RDF

decisions.decision: S01-S04 parallelizable — no inter-model dependencies
decisions.choice: Each model slice can execute independently. Cross-model verification deferred to S05.
decisions.rationale: Models must work standalone by design. Cross-model edges use shared gist hierarchy, not direct model-to-model references. Parallel execution cuts calendar time.

decisions.decision: basic-pkm v2 is additive-only, no Event type in v2.0
decisions.choice: v2.0 adds Task and Milestone only. Event type (bpkm:Event) deferred — the design doc's Calendar Hub section is forward-looking and depends on calendar provider apps (M016+).
decisions.rationale: Event type has recurrence (RRULE), attendees, and timezone complexity. Without a calendar provider app to exercise it, it's dead schema. Ship what's usable now.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add Event type when calendar provider apps are built

decisions.decision: Validation rules use sh:sparql SPARQLConstraint on separate NodeShapes
decisions.choice: Validation-only rules (warnings) placed in rules/*.ttl on dedicated NodeShapes with sh:severity sh:Warning, separate from inference SPARQLRule NodeShapes
decisions.rationale: pyshacl requires severity on parent NodeShape, not constraint node. Mixing inference and validation on one shape causes unpredictable behavior. Separate shapes is the proven pattern.

decisions.decision: Seed data pre-populates both sides of owl:inverseOf pairs
decisions.choice: Forward and inverse sides both present in seed JSON-LD. Inference produces 0 new triples for seed data but inverse properties display correctly without inference.
decisions.rationale: Matches basic-pkm and PPV pattern. Ensures data appears correctly even if inference hasn't run yet. Inference correctness tested by adding objects with only one side and checking materialization.

decisions.decision: Layout-only personas for v1 — no settings overrides
decisions.choice: Personas store dockview layout JSON + sidebar panel positions + explorer mode. No theme, font size, or other settings.
decisions.rationale: Reduces scope and complexity. Settings overrides can layer on later without breaking the persona API. Core value is layout switching.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add settings overrides if users request

decisions.decision: Dedicated `personas` table, not `user_settings` key-value
decisions.choice: New `personas` table with proper schema following DashboardSpec model pattern
decisions.rationale: Personas have CRUD lifecycle + activation semantics that don't fit key-value storage. Dedicated table enables proper FK, indexing, and schema evolution.

decisions.decision: Explicit save only — no auto-save to server on layout change
decisions.choice: Save current persona state on: explicit "Save" action, before switching to another persona, on `beforeunload`. No server save on `onDidLayoutChange`.
decisions.rationale: `onDidLayoutChange` fires on every panel resize/move — auto-saving would create excessive writes. localStorage auto-save continues independently for crash recovery.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add debounced auto-save if users request

decisions.decision: How to handle auth rate limiting in E2E test environments
decisions.choice: Added RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED env var (default true) passed to slowapi Limiter's enabled parameter. Set to false in docker-compose.test.yml. Rate-limiting E2E test updated to skip gracefully when disabled.
decisions.rationale: E2E auth fixtures create sessions rapidly (one per test), exhausting the 5/minute magic-link rate limit and causing cascading test failures. Disabling rate limiting in test stack is cleaner than increasing limits or adding delays. Production defaults remain unchanged (enabled=true).

decisions.decision: Dual-auth dependency approach for M013 API endpoints
decisions.choice: New `get_current_user_or_api` dependency that tries session cookie first, then Bearer token via existing AuthService.verify_api_token(). Existing `get_current_user` left unchanged for htmx routes.
decisions.rationale: External clients (browser extension) send Bearer tokens; htmx frontend sends cookies. Both must work on the same endpoints. Cookie-first ordering means the htmx frontend path is unchanged. AuthService.verify_api_token() already exists and is tested — no new auth logic needed, only wiring.

decisions.decision: SHACL shape JSON serialization strategy
decisions.choice: Shape serialization via dataclasses.asdict() mapped to Pydantic response models. No Pydantic migration of ShapesService internals.
decisions.rationale: Research confirmed PropertyShape/PropertyGroup/NodeShapeForm are plain Python dataclasses with simple types (str, int, float, list[str], None). dataclasses.asdict() serializes them cleanly — no custom serializers needed. Pydantic models on the response side provide OpenAPI docs and validation. Migrating ShapesService internals to Pydantic would be high-risk refactoring with no benefit to M013.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if ShapesService internals need Pydantic for other reasons

decisions.decision: CORS policy for API endpoints
decisions.choice: CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on all `/api/` and `/.well-known/sempkm` responses via nginx headers. No origin registration required.
decisions.rationale: SemPKM is self-hosted — the user controls their instance. Requiring extension origin registration adds complexity with no security benefit for local instances. Browser extensions have unpredictable origins (chrome-extension://random-id). Wildcard CORS is standard for local APIs. Can add configurable origin restrictions later for cloud-hosted instances.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add configurable CORS origins for cloud instances

decisions.decision: Context-query scope — literal matches only for v1
decisions.choice: Context-query v1 searches literal values only (URL exact match via SPARQL FILTER + FTS keyword search). No edge traversal.
decisions.rationale: URL matching (find objects containing a given URL as a property value) and FTS keyword matching (existing LuceneSail) cover the primary browser extension use case. Edge traversal (objects linked to matching objects) adds SPARQL complexity and potentially noisy results. Ship the simple version; add traversal later if needed.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add edge traversal when browser extension Phase 2 (M015) needs it

decisions.decision: How to handle 401 responses for JSON API endpoints outside /api/ prefix
decisions.choice: Extend _is_html_route() in main.py to exclude /.well-known/ paths alongside /api/, so 401 responses return JSON instead of 302 redirects
decisions.rationale: The exception handler converts 401s to 302 login redirects for HTML routes. Discovery endpoints at /.well-known/ are JSON APIs that must return structured error responses. Any future JSON API path prefix outside /api/ must also be added to the _is_html_route exclusion list.

decisions.decision: How /api/types endpoint accesses IconService
decisions.choice: Create IconService ad-hoc in endpoint handler (matching codebase pattern) rather than expecting app.state.icon_service
decisions.rationale: IconService is instantiated inline everywhere in the codebase (admin router, browser helpers, SPARQL router) — it's never registered on app.state. T01-T02 executor assumed app.state wiring, causing runtime 500. Fixed by following existing pattern: `IconService(models_dir=_MODELS_DIR)` with user_type_icons from app.state.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if IconService is centralized on app.state in a future refactor

decisions.decision: Backend auth approach for commands endpoint to support browser extension
decisions.choice: Create `require_role_or_api(*roles)` factory in `dependencies.py` that chains to `get_current_user_or_api` instead of `get_current_user`. Update `POST /api/commands` to use it. Leave existing `require_role` unchanged for htmx routes.
decisions.rationale: Parallel factory avoids breaking existing htmx routes (which rely on cookie-only `require_role`). The `get_current_user_or_api` dependency already exists and is tested (M013). This is a ~20-line change with no risk to existing auth flows. Same pattern can be applied selectively to SPARQL endpoints if needed later.

decisions.decision: Extension form rendering approach — client-side vs server-rendered
decisions.choice: Client-side JS SHACL renderer (Option A from design doc). Extension fetches shape JSON from `GET /api/shapes/{type_iri}` and renders forms in vanilla JS. No server-side HTML rendering for extension forms.
decisions.rationale: Avoids a network round-trip for form HTML, enables form rendering from cached shapes (works offline-ish), keeps the extension self-contained with no dependency on server-rendered partials. The JS renderer handles the common SHACL property types used in standard Mental Models — not every edge case. Reference implementation is the 205-line Jinja2 `_field.html` macro.

decisions.decision: Relationship picker search backend — context-query vs SPARQL endpoint
decisions.choice: Use context-query endpoint (`POST /api/context-query`) for relationship picker search in v1. Skip SPARQL endpoint Bearer auth fix — not needed for Phase 1.
decisions.rationale: Context-query already supports Bearer auth (M013). Adding Bearer auth to 19 SPARQL router endpoints is high-effort with low Phase 1 benefit. Context-query returns objects with IRIs, labels, and types — sufficient for relationship search. Client-side type filtering is acceptable for v1 result sets. SPARQL auth can be added in Phase 2 (M015) if needed.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add SPARQL Bearer auth when Phase 2 (M015) needs flexible queries

decisions.decision: Extension distribution method for Phase 1
decisions.choice: Sideload-only distribution for Phase 1. No Chrome Web Store or Firefox Add-ons submission.
decisions.rationale: Web Store review adds latency, code review requirements, and privacy disclosures. `http://localhost:*/*` in host_permissions may be rejected. Sideloading is sufficient for self-hosted users and development iteration. Web Store submission planned for later when stable.
decisions.revisable: Yes — submit to Web Store once stable

decisions.decision: Extension tech stack and build approach
decisions.choice: Vanilla JS only — no React, Vue, or build step. Plain HTML/CSS/JS in the extension directory. No bundler, no transpiler, no npm.
decisions.rationale: Chrome MV3 Content Security Policy forbids `eval()` and inline scripts. A build step adds complexity for a <2k LOC extension. Vanilla JS is consistent with the SemPKM frontend (htmx + vanilla JS). The SHACL renderer is imperative DOM manipulation which is natural in vanilla JS. No framework dependency to manage or update.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add build step if extension grows beyond Phase 1 scope

decisions.decision: Object + edge creation sequencing in extension
decisions.choice: Two-step sequential creation: object.create first → get IRI from response → edge.create second. No client-side IRI minting.
decisions.rationale: Client-side IRI minting requires replicating `mint_object_iri` logic and is fragile if the minting scheme changes. Two-step sequential is simpler, guaranteed correct, and the latency of two API calls is negligible for a user-initiated save action. If the first succeeds but the second fails, the user has an object without the relationship — show a clear error and let them retry.
decisions.revisable: Yes — switch to batch with client-minted IRIs if latency becomes an issue

decisions.decision: App uninstall triplestore data cleanup strategy
decisions.choice: Best-effort SPARQL cleanup (try/except with WARNING log). Uninstall proceeds even if triplestore queries fail. Three queries: DELETE subjects with app IRI prefix, DELETE objects with app IRI prefix, CLEAR app state graph.
decisions.rationale: Uninstall must never be blocked by a transient triplestore error. Orphaned triples are harmless (namespaced under urn:sempkm:app:{id}:). Admin can re-run cleanup manually if needed. The alternative — rolling back the DB deletion on SPARQL failure — would leave the system in an inconsistent state where the app row exists but the process is already stopped.

decisions.decision: IRI prefix enforcement scope in SDK CommandClient
decisions.choice: _check_iri_prefix() only enforces prefix on urn:sempkm:app:* and urn:sempkm:data:* namespaces. Model types (urn:sempkm:model:*), user-types (urn:sempkm:user-types:*), and standard vocabularies (http://, https://) pass through unchecked.
decisions.rationale: The original implementation rejected ALL IRIs not matching the app's own prefix, blocking apps from referencing model-defined types (the #1 platform risk for M010). Scoping enforcement to only app/data namespaces preserves sandboxing while allowing legitimate cross-namespace references.

decisions.decision: RSS article IRI minting strategy
decisions.choice: Article IRI minted via SHA-256 hash of (feed_iri + entry_id) producing urn:sempkm:app:rss-reader:article-{hash16}
decisions.rationale: Using feed_iri (not feed_url) makes IRIs stable even if the feed URL redirects. The feed_iri is the canonical subscription object IRI, which is fixed. SHA-256 prevents collision while keeping IRIs deterministic for dedup.

decisions.decision: FeedSubscription browser visibility in rss-feeds model
decisions.choice: FeedSubscription has browserVisible: false in the rss-feeds model manifest
decisions.rationale: FeedSubscriptions are managed by the RSS reader app, not manually created by users. Showing them in the object browser would clutter the user's workspace with implementation-detail objects. They remain SPARQL-queryable and editable by the app.

decisions.decision: Subscription unsubscribe strategy for RSS feeds
decisions.choice: Soft-delete via isActive=False patch on FeedSubscription, not hard delete
decisions.rationale: Existing articles reference their feed subscription IRI via rss:fromFeed. Hard-deleting the subscription would orphan those references. Soft-delete preserves article provenance chain while preventing future polling. Admin can still query inactive subscriptions via SPARQL.
decisions.revisable: Yes — switch to hard delete + cascade if article cleanup is implemented

decisions.decision: Navigate command enrichment for app pages in command palette
decisions.choice: commands_list() iterates manifest.ui.pages comparing page.path == cmd.path; on match adds appId and pageId to JSON. JS handler branches on cmd.appId to call openAppPageTab() instead of window.location.href
decisions.rationale: Exact path matching (no prefix/fuzzy) is simple and correct — app pages have unique paths. Adding appId/pageId to the JSON response lets the frontend make the right choice (dockview tab vs full navigation) without hardcoding app-specific logic in JS. This pattern works for all future apps with navigate commands.

decisions.decision: FeedSubscription browserVisible setting
decisions.choice: FeedSubscription has `browserVisible: false` in rss-feeds model manifest — hidden from object browser
decisions.rationale: FeedSubscriptions are managed by the RSS reader app, not by users directly. Showing them in the object browser would clutter the UI with infrastructure objects. They remain queryable via SPARQL and linkable via edges, just not browsable.
decisions.revisable: Yes — make visible if users need to manually manage subscriptions

decisions.decision: Feed format dispatch strategy for RSS reader
decisions.choice: parse_feed_content() dispatches by HTTP Content-Type: JSON types → custom parse_json_feed() parser, all XML types → feedparser. JSON Feed entries are normalized to SimpleNamespace objects with feedparser-compatible attribute names.
decisions.rationale: feedparser doesn't support JSON Feed format. A content-type dispatcher keeps the parsing layer format-agnostic — callers don't need to know whether the feed was RSS, Atom, or JSON Feed. SimpleNamespace provides attribute access (.title, .link) matching feedparser's FeedParserDict, so entry_to_article() works identically for all formats.

decisions.decision: trafilatura optional dependency strategy for article content extraction
decisions.choice: Module-level try/except import guard with HAS_TRAFILATURA boolean flag. When trafilatura is not installed, extract_article_content() returns None immediately (graceful degradation). Feed summary is used as fallback content.
decisions.rationale: trafilatura has heavy C extension dependencies (lxml). Making it optional ensures the RSS reader app starts and functions even if trafilatura fails to install in the Docker container. The HAS_TRAFILATURA flag is inspectable at runtime for diagnostics. Feed-provided summaries are always available as fallback content.
decisions.revisable: Yes — make required once Docker build is proven stable with trafilatura

decisions.decision: Conditional GET (ETag/Last-Modified) for feed polling bandwidth optimization
decisions.choice: fetch_feed() sends If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since headers from stored per-subscription etag/lastModifiedHeader values. On 304, returns (None, headers, 304) — caller skips parsing. On success, update_subscription_state() persists new etag/lastModified for next cycle.
decisions.rationale: Polling feeds every 5 minutes generates redundant traffic when feed content hasn't changed. Conditional GET lets servers return 304 Not Modified (no body), saving bandwidth and parsing time. Per-subscription state stored as RDF predicates on FeedSubscription objects so conditional GET state persists across app restarts.

decisions.decision: RSS Reader user guide chapter number
decisions.choice: Numbered as Chapter 32 (not Chapter 30 as originally planned) — chapters 30 (Workspace Personas) and 31 (API Surface) already existed when S06 executed
decisions.rationale: The S06 plan assumed ch.29 was the last numbered chapter, but M012/S04 and M013/S03 had already created chapters 30 and 31 respectively. Maintaining sequential numbering required ch.32. Navigation chain adjusted: ch.31 → ch.32 → Appendix A.

decisions.decision: Title extraction strategy for dynamic SHACL forms in extension popup
decisions.choice: 4-priority cascade: (1) property path containing "title" or "dcterms:title", (2) path containing "name" (firstName, lastName), (3) first required field value, (4) any non-empty value. Concatenates name parts for CRM-style types.
decisions.rationale: Different Mental Model types use different title conventions — basic-pkm uses dcterms:title, CRM Contact has firstName/lastName but no title field, Task has dcterms:title. A cascade handles all cases without type-specific branching. Falls through gracefully — validation only requires a non-empty title, the cascade almost always finds something.

decisions.decision: Content script injection strategy for browser extension page data extraction
decisions.choice: chrome.scripting.executeScript({func: extractPageData}) with imported function reference — single return value, no message-passing, no persistent content script
decisions.rationale: Cleaner than {files:} approach which requires message-passing to get data back. The func parameter serializes/deserializes the function body, so the extractor must be fully self-contained (var declarations, no closures, no imports). This avoids a persistent content script that would run on every page load. The popup injects on-demand only when opened.

decisions.decision: Context menu to popup data bridge for "Save to SemPKM" right-click action
decisions.choice: Context menu handler stores {selectionText, pageUrl, pageTitle} in chrome.storage.session, then opens popup via chrome.action.openPopup(). Popup checks session storage on init, consumes and clears data.
decisions.rationale: Service worker and popup are separate execution contexts — no shared memory. chrome.storage.session is ephemeral (cleared on browser restart), fast, and doesn't pollute sync storage. The consume-and-clear pattern prevents stale data from affecting subsequent popup opens. chrome.action.openPopup() is the standard MV3 approach; chrome.windows.create() fallback handles the case where openPopup() isn't available.

decisions.decision: Schema.org to SHACL form property mapping priority
decisions.choice: Cross-namespace mappings (CROSS_NS_MAP) take priority over direct schema.org namespace matches in mapSchemaOrgToFormValues — first-write-wins prevents overwriting specific mappings with generic ones
decisions.rationale: A schema.org Person has both schema:givenName and a CRM model might have crm:firstName. The cross-namespace map explicitly encodes domain-specific intent (givenName → crm:firstName), which should take priority over a generic direct-namespace match. First-write-wins means the cross-namespace mapping is checked first, and if it populates a path, the direct match skips it.

decisions.decision: Edge creation error handling strategy in extension two-step save
decisions.choice: Per-edge try/catch with warning toast showing failure count — edge failures never block object creation success
decisions.rationale: Object creation is the primary user intent. Edges are supplementary relationship metadata. If the API is partially available or a single edge call fails due to a transient error, losing the entire object would be worse than losing a relationship. The user sees a clear warning toast with the failure count, so they know to re-add the relationship manually. Console logs identify exactly which edge failed for debugging.

decisions.decision: Sidebar implementation strategy — Chrome Side Panel API over content-script Shadow DOM injection
decisions.choice: Use Chrome's native `chrome.sidePanel` API for Chrome and `sidebar_action` manifest key for Firefox. Sidebar HTML/JS/CSS shared between both browsers.
decisions.rationale: Side Panel API provides a dedicated browser surface that doesn't conflict with page CSS, persists across navigation, and has full access to Chrome extension APIs. Shadow DOM injection requires fighting with arbitrary page CSS, doesn't persist across navigation, and has limited API access. The cross-browser gap is manageable with the existing dual-manifest pattern from M014.

decisions.decision: Popup and sidebar coexistence strategy — keep popup for capture, sidebar for context
decisions.choice: Do NOT use `sidePanel.setPanelBehavior({openPanelOnActionClick: true})` which replaces the popup. Instead, open sidebar programmatically via Alt+K keyboard shortcut (new `commands` entry) or from a "Show Context" button inside the popup. Icon click continues to open the capture popup.
decisions.rationale: Users need both flows: quick capture (popup via icon click / Alt+S) and context browsing (sidebar via Alt+K). Replacing one with the other reduces functionality. Separate entry points serve distinct user intents.

decisions.decision: Context query signal splitting — separate URL, title, and keywords fields
decisions.choice: Add `contextQuery({url, title, keywords})` method to SemPKMClient that sends each field separately to POST /api/context-query, replacing the single-string `searchObjects()` approach
decisions.rationale: The context-query endpoint already accepts `url`, `title`, and `keywords` as separate fields. Sending the same string as both title and keywords (current behavior) misses URL matching entirely and produces suboptimal keyword results. Separate signals enable URL exact match (highest confidence) alongside keyword search.

decisions.decision: Client-side result ranking strategy — URL match > title match > keyword match
decisions.choice: Results ranked on the extension side before rendering: URL matches first (exact property match), then title matches, then keyword matches. Truncate to top 10.
decisions.rationale: The context-query endpoint returns flat results with match_type field but no ranking. Client-side ranking is simpler than modifying the backend endpoint and can be tuned per-UI without API changes. Top 10 prevents sidebar overflow from false positives.
decisions.revisable: Yes — move ranking to backend if needed across multiple clients

decisions.decision: Service worker context cache — in-memory Map with LRU eviction, no persistence
decisions.choice: URL→results cache as a plain Map in service worker memory. Max 100 entries with LRU eviction. Lost on service worker termination (MV3 lifecycle). No chrome.storage persistence.
decisions.rationale: Cache is a performance optimization, not a correctness requirement. Re-querying on cache miss is cheap against a local instance. Persisting to chrome.storage would add read/write latency and storage management for ephemeral data. MV3 service workers restart cleanly.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add chrome.storage.session persistence if re-query latency is noticeable

decisions.decision: Linear sync app authentication strategy — OAuth vs API key
decisions.choice: Support both OAuth 2.0 (with mandatory refresh tokens) and personal API key auth. OAuth for multi-user/production, API key for personal/local dev. API key entered in settings page; OAuth via redirect flow through app proxy callback URL.
decisions.rationale: Linear mandates refresh tokens for OAuth2 apps created since Oct 2025, with 24h access token expiry. API key auth is simpler and avoids OAuth callback routing complexity for local dev. Supporting both maximizes usability: API key for quick personal setup, OAuth for production deployments where multiple users authenticate independently.

decisions.decision: Linear sync mechanism — polling vs webhooks
decisions.choice: Polling-only for v1. No webhook endpoint. poll-tasks scheduled task fetches issues via GraphQL with updatedAt filter for delta sync.
decisions.rationale: The App Platform doesn't expose app routes to external traffic — only platform-proxied internal routes. Linear webhooks can't reach localhost for local dev. Polling with updatedAt delta cursor covers the core sync UX. Webhooks can be added when the platform gains external webhook routing.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add webhooks when platform supports external webhook routing

decisions.decision: Linear GraphQL client approach — httpx direct vs gql library
decisions.choice: Use httpx directly via SDK's HttpClient for GraphQL POST requests to https://api.linear.app/graphql. No gql library.
decisions.rationale: Linear's GraphQL API is a single POST endpoint. The SDK's HttpClient already wraps httpx with domain enforcement. Adding the gql library brings dependency weight (graphql-core, etc.) for no benefit over raw POST with JSON query strings. Query construction is simpler as string templates with variable interpolation.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add gql if query complexity warrants it

decisions.decision: Linear sync conflict resolution strategy
decisions.choice: Status: provider wins (Linear state.type is authoritative). Title/description: last-write-wins based on dcterms:modified vs Linear updatedAt. Compare lastSyncedAt to detect which side changed.
decisions.rationale: Linear's state.type enum is a cleaner status model than free-text — letting the provider win for status avoids lossy round-trips. For title/description, last-write-wins is pragmatic for a single-user self-hosted app where true conflicts are rare. lastSyncedAt timestamp comparison detects which side changed since last sync.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add field-level merge if multi-user conflicts become common

decisions.decision: Linear app unit test approach — importlib loading from apps/ directory
decisions.choice: Use importlib.util.spec_from_file_location to load app modules from apps/linear-sync/services/ into backend pytest tests. Mock SDK clients (HttpClient, StateClient) with simple async classes.
decisions.rationale: App code lives in apps/ (outside backend/), not importable via normal Python paths. The test-app has no unit tests, but the research doc recommends the importlib pattern used by M010 RSS Reader. Mocking SDK clients avoids platform runtime dependencies and makes tests fast and deterministic.

decisions.decision: Sync engine bulk creation strategy for platform-minted IRIs
decisions.choice: Two-phase bulk: phase 1 submits object.create commands (no IRI needed, platform mints it), phase 2 re-queries SPARQL to discover the minted IRIs then submits body.set/edge.create commands referencing those IRIs. All commands bypass SDK's CommandClient via direct POST to /api/commands/bulk to avoid IRI prefix checking on patch/body/edge commands.
decisions.rationale: The App SDK's CommandClient enforces an IRI prefix check (urn:sempkm:app:{appId}:) on object.patch, body.set, body.diff, and edge.create commands. Platform-minted Task IRIs use urn:sempkm:object: prefix, which the SDK rejects. Bypassing via ctx.commands._client (the underlying httpx.AsyncClient) avoids the prefix check while still using the platform's bulk command endpoint. The two-phase approach is needed because object.create returns no IRI — the platform assigns it — so body/edge commands for new objects must wait until the IRI is discoverable via SPARQL.
decisions.revisable: Yes — once the SDK supports an IRI prefix override or the platform returns created IRIs in bulk response

decisions.decision: Push sync loop prevention mechanism
decisions.choice: pull_sync compares issue updatedAt against task's bpkm:lastSyncedAt — skips issues where updatedAt ≤ lastSyncedAt. String comparison on ISO-8601 timestamps. push_sync updates lastSyncedAt after each successful issueUpdate mutation.
decisions.rationale: When push_sync sends a change to Linear, the next poll sees that issue as updated. Without loop detection, pull_sync would re-import the pushed change. Comparing timestamps is simple and correct because both Linear updatedAt and bpkm:lastSyncedAt use ISO-8601 format where lexicographic ordering equals temporal ordering. lastSyncedAt is set after the mutation completes, so the next poll's updatedAt will be ≤ lastSyncedAt for push-originated changes.
decisions.revisable: Yes — may need server-side mutation tracking if timestamp granularity causes issues

decisions.decision: GitHub sync authentication — PAT-only for v1, no OAuth App
decisions.choice: Personal Access Token only for v1. No GitHub OAuth App registration or OAuth code exchange flow.
decisions.rationale: PAT is simpler, matches the M016 API key path, and avoids OAuth callback routing (same localhost limitation as D200). Users create a PAT with `repo` scope in GitHub Settings. OAuth App flow adds client_id/secret management, callback URL configuration, and token refresh complexity — all for the same functional outcome (API access). Can add OAuth later if multi-user production deployments need it.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add GitHub OAuth App flow for production multi-user

decisions.decision: GitHub REST pagination — manual Link header parsing, no library
decisions.choice: Parse `Link: <url>; rel="next"` from response headers with simple regex/split. No pagination library.
decisions.rationale: Link header format is trivial (~5 lines to parse). Adding a library for one regex is overhead. httpx exposes response.headers directly. Same approach used throughout SemPKM codebase — keep it simple.

decisions.decision: PR-to-issue linking via timeline API cross-referenced events
decisions.choice: Use GET `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/timeline` to find `cross-referenced` events where `source.issue.pull_request` exists. Create `bpkm:dependsOn` edges from PR task → issue task.
