decisions.rationale: Text parsing of "Closes #42" in PR bodies is fragile (multiple variations, localization, false positives). The timeline API returns structured events that definitively identify cross-references. The `cross-referenced` event type includes the source PR reference, making link direction unambiguous.

decisions.decision: GitHub sync requirement IDs use GH- prefix
decisions.choice: New requirements numbered GH-01 through GH-07 instead of continuing SYNC- sequence
decisions.rationale: SYNC-05 through SYNC-07 are already taken by M016 (Linear sync) with different meanings. GH- prefix avoids collision and makes requirements clearly identifiable by provider. Future sync apps should follow: TD- (Todoist), AS- (Asana), JR- (Jira), etc.

decisions.decision: Google Calendar sync authentication — full OAuth 2.0, no API key alternative
decisions.choice: OAuth 2.0 code exchange with refresh tokens. Client ID/secret from Google Cloud Console. Unverified client for dev. Token refresh automatic on 401 (access tokens expire after 1h).
decisions.rationale: Google Calendar API v3 has no API key path for user-data access — OAuth is mandatory. First real OAuth in a sync app (Linear used API key D199, GitHub used PAT D206). Callback URL routes through app proxy at /app/google-calendar/_fragments/oauth-callback.

decisions.decision: Polling-only sync for Google Calendar v1, no push notification channels
decisions.choice: syncToken-based incremental polling. No webhook channels.
decisions.rationale: Same constraint as D200 — App Platform doesn't expose external webhook routes. Polling with syncToken is highly efficient (returns only changes). Push notification channels require publicly reachable URL + 7-day renewal. Polling matches M016/M017 pattern.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add push channels when platform supports external webhook routing

decisions.decision: bpkm:Event property set designed as cross-provider superset
decisions.choice: Event type includes all enum values from Google + Outlook + CalDAV even if Google doesn't use them all (e.g. showAs: out-of-office, working-elsewhere are Outlook-specific).
decisions.rationale: The Event type must serve M018 (Google), M020 (Outlook), and M021 (CalDAV). Building the superset now avoids a breaking ontology change when Outlook sync lands. Unused enum values are harmless.

decisions.decision: RSVP-only push scope for v1 — no full event creation/edit push
decisions.choice: Push sync limited to responseStatus changes. Title, description, time edits NOT pushed to Google.
decisions.rationale: Narrow push scope reduces complexity and risk. RSVP is the most common bidirectional action. Full event editing push requires field-by-field conflict resolution that exceeds v1 scope. Meeting notes explicitly listed as SemPKM-only in CONTEXT.
decisions.revisable: Yes — expand push scope if users request bidirectional event editing

decisions.decision: Google Calendar requirement IDs use GCAL- prefix, Event type uses EVENT-
decisions.choice: GCAL-01 through GCAL-09 for sync app. EVENT-01 for bpkm:Event type (shared across calendar providers).
decisions.rationale: Follows D209 pattern — provider-specific prefix avoids collision. EVENT-01 is provider-neutral because the type serves Google, Outlook, and CalDAV.

decisions.decision: Jira status normalization strategy
decisions.choice: Always use statusCategory.key (new/indeterminate/done) for mapping, never status.name. Store status.name in bpkm:externalStatus for display.
decisions.rationale: Status names are arbitrarily customizable per Jira project. statusCategory.key is the only reliable normalization point — maps every custom status to exactly one of three categories. This is Jira's designed abstraction for cross-project status comparison.

decisions.decision: Jira sync requirement ID prefix
decisions.choice: Requirements numbered JIRA-01 through JIRA-12 following D209 (GH-) and D230 (ASANA-) provider-specific prefix pattern.
decisions.rationale: Provider-specific prefix avoids collision and makes requirements identifiable by provider.

decisions.decision: Jira status normalization via statusCategory.key, not status name
decisions.choice: Always use statusCategory.key (new/indeterminate/done) for status mapping, never status.name. Store status.name in bpkm:externalStatus for display.
decisions.rationale: Status names are arbitrarily customizable per Jira project ("In Review", "QA Testing", etc.). statusCategory.key is the only reliable normalization point — maps every custom status to exactly one of three categories. This is Jira's designed abstraction for cross-project status comparison.

decisions.decision: Jira sync authentication — API token (email + token as Basic auth) for v1, no OAuth 2.0 3LO
decisions.choice: API token only. User generates token at id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens. Stored as email + token pair via StateClient. Basic auth header: base64(email:token).
decisions.rationale: Atlassian OAuth 2.0 (3LO) requires registering a Jira app with Atlassian developer console, managing client_id/secret, handling complex callback routing, and scope negotiation. API token is simpler and matches D206 (GitHub PAT) pattern. Sufficient for self-hosted single-user use. OAuth can be added in v2.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add OAuth 2.0 3LO for multi-user production

decisions.decision: Push sync limited to title/description/priority for v1 — no status transitions
decisions.choice: Push sync handles title and priority only. No status transition push — Jira requires discovering valid workflow transitions per issue via GET /transitions then POST /transitions with transition ID.
decisions.rationale: Jira requires valid transition IDs for status changes (unlike Linear/GitHub where you set any status directly). Per-project transition discovery and validation is a separate concern from basic field sync. Title/description/priority PATCH is sufficient for v1 bidirectional capability.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add status transition push in v2

decisions.decision: Jira person resolution requires extra API call per unique accountId
decisions.choice: Jira v3 API uses opaque accountId (not email). Getting email requires GET /rest/api/3/user?accountId=X. Cache aggressively via PersonMatcher LRU cache — each unique user looked up once per sync run.
decisions.rationale: Jira's GDPR-compliant API removed email from issue response data. The extra API call is unavoidable but the LRU cache (same pattern as all other sync apps) means each unique user is looked up only once per sync run.

decisions.decision: ADF ↔ Markdown conversion — custom recursive converter, not library
decisions.choice: Hand-roll a ~400-line recursive converter covering ~12 common ADF node types (paragraph, heading, bulletList, orderedList, codeBlock, blockquote, table, text with marks, mention, inlineCard, mediaGroup, rule) plus reverse direction. Unknown node types emit [unsupported: {type}] placeholder.
decisions.rationale: No well-maintained Python ADF↔MD library exists. The node types are well-documented and finite. A focused converter covering common types is more reliable than depending on an unmaintained package. The reverse direction (MD→ADF) only needs to handle the Markdown subset SemPKM produces.
decisions.revisable: Yes — switch to library if a well-maintained one appears

decisions.decision: Jira issue link deduplication strategy for dependsOn edges
decisions.choice: Process only inwardIssue entries from "Blocks" links (the blocker→blocked direction). Skip outwardIssue to avoid creating duplicate edges.
decisions.rationale: Each Jira blocking relationship appears in both issues' issuelinks arrays — as outwardIssue on the blocker and as inwardIssue on the blocked. Processing both directions would create duplicate bpkm:dependsOn edges. Filtering to inward-only (current issue "is blocked by" the inward issue) ensures one edge per blocking relationship while maintaining the correct dependency semantics.

decisions.decision: LoopGuard as lightweight TTL cache module for echo prevention
decisions.choice: Standalone loop_guard.py with LoopGuard class tracking (item_id, column_id) → timestamp with configurable TTL (default 30s). In-memory only.
decisions.rationale: Monday.com has no webhook suppression. For v1 polling, push→poll echo occurs within same process lifetime. Simple in-memory TTL dict is sufficient and highly testable.
decisions.revisable: Yes — promote to shared platform utility if multiple apps need echo prevention

decisions.decision: Monday.com column mapping per-board storage keys
decisions.choice: Column mapping stored at `column_mapping_{board_id}` and label mapping at `label_mapping_{board_id}` as JSON in settings. Label mapping contains nested `status_label_mapping` and `priority_label_mapping` sub-dicts.
decisions.rationale: Monday.com boards are independently configurable — each board has unique columns, status labels, and priority labels. Per-board keys allow a single app installation to sync multiple boards with different mapping configurations. Follows the D228 "configure before sync" pattern established by Asana. Nested label mapping structure keeps status and priority mappings co-located per board for atomic read/write.

decisions.decision: Monday.com group→taskGroup sourced from item.group, not column_values
decisions.choice: Group title sourced from `item["group"]["title"]` in GraphQL response. Subitems fetched via separate `get_subitems(item_ids)` call. Group is structural metadata, not a column value.
decisions.rationale: Monday.com groups are structural containers, not user-configurable columns. They appear in the items query under `group { id title }` but are absent from `column_values`. Using `item.group.title` directly (not via column mapping) is correct because the group assignment comes from item placement, not from a column value the user can remap. Similarly, subitems are separate items requiring a distinct API call, matching the structural relationship model.

decisions.decision: DEMO_MODE env var for anonymous access — synthetic guest user bypass
decisions.choice: `DEMO_MODE=true` env var makes `get_current_user` return a synthetic read-only guest user without session/cookie. No login page shown.
decisions.rationale: Option B from research — cleaner than pre-seeded demo user with auto-login cookie. Synthetic user gets `role: "guest"` which already has restricted permissions. Combined with nginx write-blocking, this is defense-in-depth. ~15 lines in auth/dependencies.py, no new endpoints needed.

decisions.decision: Read-only enforcement via nginx default-deny on non-GET methods
decisions.choice: Block all POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH at nginx level for all routes except health check. Return 403 JSON `{"error": "Demo instance is read-only"}`.
decisions.rationale: Default-deny is safer than endpoint-by-endpoint allowlisting — missing one POST route allows data corruption across visitors. Research identified 20+ mutation endpoints; blocking by HTTP method catches all current and future write routes with ~10 lines of nginx config.

decisions.decision: Caddy reverse proxy for SSL termination, not nginx SSL config
decisions.choice: Caddy runs on host, proxies to Docker's nginx on port 3000. Handles Let's Encrypt automatically with zero config.
decisions.rationale: Avoids modifying nginx.conf for SSL — Caddy's automatic HTTPS is simpler than Let's Encrypt + certbot + nginx SSL blocks. Caddy also handles certificate renewal automatically. Keeps the demo nginx.conf identical to the local dev config.

decisions.decision: Demo requirement IDs use DEMO- prefix
decisions.choice: 10 requirements numbered DEMO-01 through DEMO-10 covering anonymous access, read-only, sample data, tour, dashboard, CTA, deployment, reset, monitoring, validation.
decisions.rationale: Follows established provider-specific prefix convention (D209, D214, D216, D221, D226, D230, D234).

decisions.decision: M025 is deployment + content — no new platform features
decisions.choice: DEMO_MODE is a configuration flag (~15 lines), not a feature. Same Docker Compose 3-service stack. No new containers except optional Caddy for SSL.
decisions.rationale: Research confirmed every pattern needed (Driver.js tours, dashboard builder, seed data JSON-LD) is already exercised. Platform feature changes would increase risk for no benefit.

decisions.decision: How to bypass FastAPI Depends() chain in get_current_user for DEMO_MODE
decisions.choice: Replaced Depends(get_session_token) with inline Cookie(None) extraction in get_current_user, so demo_mode check runs before any 401 can fire. get_session_token preserved for logout endpoint.
decisions.rationale: FastAPI evaluates Depends() arguments before the function body runs. The old get_session_token dependency raises 401 when no cookie is present, which would fire before any demo_mode check in the function body. Inlining the cookie extraction as an optional parameter lets the function body execute first, where the demo_mode guard returns the synthetic user immediately.

decisions.decision: How to handle setup wizard redirect in DEMO_MODE
decisions.choice: Short-circuit /api/auth/status to return setup_complete=true, setup_mode=false when DEMO_MODE=true
decisions.rationale: DEMO_MODE auth bypass (T01) prevents 401s but doesn't prevent the client-side JS setup wizard redirect. Fresh demo instances have setup_mode=true, causing auth.js to redirect to /setup.html before auth can take effect. The fix is at the status endpoint (not in JS or middleware) because it's the single source of truth the client checks, and it avoids modifying shared frontend code.

decisions.decision: nginx JSON response for write-blocking in demo mode
decisions.choice: error_page 495 + named @read_only location pattern — custom error code 495 (unused by nginx) triggers internal redirect to named location that sets default_type application/json and returns 403 with JSON body
decisions.rationale: Bare `return 403` inside nginx `if` blocks always sends `text/plain` content-type — there's no way to set Content-Type: application/json with that pattern. The `limit_except` directive doesn't work at server level. The error_page + named location approach is the canonical nginx solution for returning JSON error responses from method guards.

decisions.decision: How the demo seed script bypasses HTTP auth and nginx write-blocking
decisions.choice: Script runs inside the API container via `docker compose exec` using direct Python module imports (TriplestoreClient, EventStore, ModelService) — bypasses both HTTP auth and nginx
decisions.rationale: Three alternatives were considered: (1) HTTP API calls to port 8902 (bypasses nginx but requires owner auth — DEMO_MODE guest user lacks install/command permissions), (2) two-phase deployment (start without DEMO_MODE, seed, restart with DEMO_MODE — fragile, compose file hardcodes DEMO_MODE=true), (3) direct module imports inside container (works regardless of DEMO_MODE since model install and EventStore.commit don't check the flag). Option 3 is simplest and most reliable — follows the same pattern as ensure_starter_model() at app startup.

decisions.decision: Deterministic UUID for demo dashboard shared between tour JS and seed script
decisions.choice: Well-known UUID `aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee` hardcoded in both `tutorials.js` (tour step 6) and `seed-demo-data.py` (Phase 4/5 dashboard creation)
decisions.rationale: The demo tour's step 6 calls `openDashboardTab(dashboardId, name)` which needs to know the dashboard ID at JS runtime. Using a deterministic UUID rather than discovering it at runtime (which would need an API call) keeps the tour code simple and avoids async complexity. The seed script uses the same UUID when creating the dashboard, making it a shared constant. This is a pattern already used in the codebase (demo user UUID `00000000-...`).

decisions.decision: No static site generator — vanilla HTML/CSS/JS for homepage rewrite
decisions.choice: Rewrite docs/index.html in-place with vanilla HTML/CSS/JS. Extract shared CSS to docs/styles.css. Add 3 persona sub-pages as separate HTML files. No Jekyll, Hugo, Astro, or any SSG.
decisions.rationale: The existing docs/ directory is served directly by GitHub Pages with no build step. This is consistent with the project's "no build step" frontend philosophy (htmx + vanilla JS). At most 4 HTML files sharing one CSS file — an SSG adds tooling complexity for negligible benefit.

decisions.decision: Homepage messaging grounded in USER-CONVERSION-STRATEGY.md, not invented
decisions.choice: All hero copy, persona paths, competitive positioning, and feature framing derived from .gsd/design/USER-CONVERSION-STRATEGY.md. No ad-hoc marketing copy.
decisions.rationale: The strategy doc contains researched competitive analysis, persona definitions, and messaging shifts. Using it as the content source ensures consistency and avoids subjective copywriting. Can iterate on copy post-launch based on user feedback.

decisions.decision: SITE requirement IDs for homepage-specific requirements
decisions.choice: New requirements SITE-01 through SITE-07 covering homepage rewrite, persona paths, competitive positioning, domain kits, screenshots, mobile/performance, and SEO.
decisions.rationale: These are new scope not covered by existing requirements. SITE- prefix clearly identifies them as marketing site concerns separate from app functionality. SITE-04 through SITE-07 are quality attributes naturally embedded in the main work.

decisions.decision: Screenshots captured from M025 demo stack, not fresh Docker build
decisions.choice: Use the M025 demo Docker stack (docker-compose.demo.yml with seed data) as the screenshot source, not a dev stack or production instance.
decisions.rationale: The demo stack has 74 pre-populated objects across 4 Mental Models, a demo dashboard, and represents the "best foot forward" state of the app. Screenshots from this stack match what the "Try the Demo" CTA links to.

decisions.decision: Notion importer follows Obsidian pattern — parallel module, not shared imports/ extraction
decisions.choice: New `backend/app/notion/` module (scanner, executor, router, models, broadcast) mirroring `backend/app/obsidian/` structure. Copy-and-adapt broadcast.py rather than extracting shared `imports/` module.
decisions.rationale: Copy-and-adapt is lower risk than refactoring the working Obsidian importer. Both modules are small (~5 files each). Shared extraction can happen in a follow-up if a third importer is added.
decisions.revisable: Yes — extract shared imports/ module if a third importer is built

decisions.decision: Classify step deferred — auto-classify databases as structured, standalone pages as content
decisions.choice: Research doc proposes a 5-way classification step (structured/content/dashboard/skip/reference). M027 auto-classifies: CSV databases = structured types, standalone .md pages = content (Notes). Users can skip individual items in the type mapping step.
decisions.rationale: Classification adds wizard complexity without proportional value for v1. Auto-classification covers 90%+ of real Notion exports. Users who need finer control can skip items. Dashboard/rollup classification deferred per CONTEXT.md scope.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add explicit classification step if user feedback shows auto-classify is insufficient

decisions.decision: NOTION requirement IDs for Notion import
decisions.choice: 3 requirements: NOTION-01 (ZIP import), NOTION-02 (database→type mapping), NOTION-03 (relation→edge resolution). NOTION-01 was already registered as deferred — M027 activates it.
decisions.rationale: Follows provider-specific prefix convention. NOTION-01 already exists in REQUIREMENTS.md as deferred.

decisions.decision: CSV parsing uses stdlib csv with utf-8-sig encoding, dates via python-dateutil
decisions.choice: Python stdlib `csv` module with `encoding='utf-8-sig'` for BOM handling. Date parsing via `dateutil.parser.parse()` (already in deps). No new dependencies.
decisions.rationale: Notion exports CSVs in UTF-8 with BOM. dateutil handles locale-dependent date formats robustly. Both are proven tools already in the project.

decisions.decision: Relation resolution is title-based with ambiguity warnings
decisions.choice: CSV exports contain page title strings, not Notion IDs. Scanner detects relations by checking if column values are a subset (>80%) of another DB's row titles. Executor resolves by title→IRI dict lookup after Pass 1. Duplicate titles produce warnings in import summary, with first-match behavior.
decisions.rationale: This is a fundamental limitation of Notion's ZIP export format — no alternative exists for ZIP-only import. The 80% heuristic for detection is conservative. Warning users about ambiguous matches is the right UX — they can fix duplicates before re-importing.
decisions.revisable: Yes — switch to ID-based resolution when Notion API integration is added

decisions.decision: QUIC/HTTP/3 for self-hosted Docker deployment
decisions.choice: Defer — nginx:stable-alpine lacks HTTP/3 support. Document rationale, revisit when nginx stable adds HTTP/3 or Caddy migration is separately motivated.
decisions.rationale: nginx:stable-alpine does NOT include HTTP/3 module (requires --with-http_v3_module + BoringSSL). nginx:mainline-alpine has experimental HTTP/3 but not stable. Self-hosted single-user tool over localhost gets minimal benefit from QUIC multiplexing and 0-RTT. HTTP/2 over h2c (cleartext) has limited browser support. Caddy supports HTTP/3 out of the box and is already used for the demo instance (D246), but switching the main Docker stack is a separate decision with its own trade-offs. Cost of implementing exceeds benefit for the current deployment model.
decisions.revisable: Yes — revisit when nginx:stable-alpine adds HTTP/3 or Caddy migration is separately motivated

decisions.decision: Cross-model data quality rule placement — attach to basic-pkm with broad target patterns
decisions.choice: Place cross-model rules (comma-in-tags, titleless objects, orphan objects) in basic-pkm's rules/basic-pkm.ttl with broad sh:targetSubjectsOf or rdfs:Resource patterns, not in a new platform rules graph
decisions.rationale: basic-pkm is auto-installed as the starter model — always present. A platform rules graph (Option A from research) would require loader changes (new graph IRI pattern, separate loading logic). Attaching to basic-pkm is zero-infrastructure and follows the existing pattern where basic-pkm already has cross-cutting rules (overdue tasks). Migrate to platform rules graph later if a non-basic-pkm-only deployment becomes possible.
decisions.revisable: Yes — migrate to platform rules graph if basic-pkm becomes optional

decisions.decision: Lint filter storage in SQLite with server-side Python filtering
decisions.choice: Three new SQLite tables (lint_suppressions, lint_dismissals, lint_presets) via Alembic migration. LintService applies Python post-filtering after SPARQL query returns results.
decisions.rationale: Suppressions/dismissals are user preferences, not knowledge graph data — SQLite is the natural home (alongside auth, favorites, personas). Server-side Python filtering is clean because the SPARQL queries for lint results are already complex; adding SQL-sourced filter lists to SPARQL would require cross-database joins (impossible). Python post-filtering is performant for typical result sets (~50-200 results).

decisions.decision: Lint filter preset schema — additive suppression model
decisions.choice: Presets store a list of suppressed rule source shape IRIs (start from "show all", suppress some). Not restrictive (start from "show none", enable some).
decisions.rationale: Additive is simpler and matches the natural "hide the noisy ones" workflow. Users start seeing everything and progressively suppress rules they don't care about. The preset captures what to hide, not what to show.
decisions.revisable: Yes — switch to restrictive if users need "show only X" workflows

decisions.decision: LINT requirement IDs for data quality linting
decisions.choice: New requirements LINT-08 through LINT-20 covering pipeline fix (LINT-08), 9 data quality rules (LINT-09 through LINT-17), and lint filter system (LINT-18 suppress, LINT-19 dismiss, LINT-20 presets). Continues from LINT-07 (last M011/v2.4 lint requirement).
decisions.rationale: LINT prefix established by v2.4 lint dashboard requirements (LINT-01 through LINT-07). Continuing the sequence maintains traceability.

decisions.decision: Orphan object rule as SHACL-AF with performance monitoring, not SavedQuery
decisions.choice: Implement orphan detection as a SHACL-AF SPARQLConstraint rule (same as other 8 rules), not as a SavedQuery. Monitor performance during S02 — if >5s on Ideaverse-scale data, convert to SavedQuery as a follow-up.
decisions.rationale: Consistency: all 9 rules use the same mechanism. Users see orphan results alongside other lint results without running a separate query. The performance concern is speculative — measure first, optimize if needed.
decisions.revisable: Yes — convert to SavedQuery if performance is unacceptable

decisions.decision: Model-declared view variant access after carousel removal
decisions.choice: View toolbar dropdown shows model-declared ViewSpecs when a type filter pill is active. Model-declared views also appear in the Saved Views folder. Two surfaces replace the single carousel.
decisions.rationale: The carousel is the ONLY current surface for model-declared ViewSpecs (VIEW-05). Simply removing it loses access to type-specific views like "Projects Table". The view toolbar already exists and is the natural home for a variant selector alongside the scope dropdown. Adding entries to Saved Views provides a second discovery path. Both approaches use existing UI patterns with no new components.

decisions.decision: M031 requirement ID prefixes and numbering
decisions.choice: Requirements numbered VIEW-08 through VIEW-14, SQ-01 through SQ-03, SPARQL-09 through SPARQL-11, ONTO-04 through ONTO-06, and DBUIX-01 through DBUIX-04. Continues existing prefix sequences for views, SPARQL, and ontology; introduces SQ- and DBUIX- for new domains.
decisions.rationale: VIEW- continues from VIEW-07 (M007). SPARQL- continues from SPARQL-08 (v2.6). ONTO- continues from ONTO-03 (M003). SQ- (Saved Queries) and DBUIX- (Dashboard/Builder UX) are new prefixes for new capability areas. 20 requirements total covering all 6 scope areas.

decisions.decision: Kanban status field discovery strategy
decisions.choice: Kanban uses bpkm:taskStatus for v1 column discovery. Falls back to a hardcoded ["todo", "in-progress", "done", "cancelled"] set. Types without status fields show an empty kanban with a message.
decisions.rationale: bpkm:taskStatus is the only status-like field with sh:in constraints in the current Mental Models. SHACL shape inspection for arbitrary status fields is complex and adds scope. Hardcoding to the known field covers the primary use case (Task kanban). Can upgrade to SHACL-based field discovery in a follow-up if other models add status fields.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add SHACL-based status field discovery when other models need kanban

decisions.decision: Multiple view instance tab ID strategy
decisions.choice: Multiple view instance tab IDs use `generic-view-{renderer}-{uuid}` format. dockview addPanel creates a new panel for each unique ID. The scope query and type filter are stored as panel params.
decisions.rationale: dockview deduplicates tabs by ID. The current `generic-view-table` ID prevents opening a second table view. Appending a UUID creates unique tabs while preserving the prefix for type identification. Scope and type filter stored as panel params so the view can re-fetch on restore. Matches the pattern used by object tabs (which use IRI-based unique IDs).

decisions.decision: Scope filter injection via SPARQL sub-select pattern
decisions.choice: Sub-select pattern: `{ SELECT ?s WHERE { <scope_filter> } }` injected into WHERE clause, with variable normalization to ?s via extract_scope_where_body()
decisions.rationale: Follows VFS build_scope_filter() pattern but normalizes saved query primary SELECT variable to ?s for consistency with view query builders. Sub-select composes well with type filters and SHACL-derived columns. Graceful degradation (render unfiltered) when scope_query is invalid avoids user-facing errors.

decisions.decision: Tab ID refinement — Date.now() for unscoped, composite key for scoped
decisions.choice: Scoped tabs use `generic-view:{renderer}:scope:{queryId}` (deduplicates same query). Unscoped tabs use `generic-view:{renderer}:{Date.now()}` (every click = new tab). Tab labels append scope name or numeric suffix.
decisions.rationale: Refines D287 (planning used UUID). Date.now() is simpler than UUID generation in browser JS and collision is impossible from user interaction. Scoped deduplication prevents redundant tabs for the same saved query. Numeric suffixes ("Table View (2)") differentiate unscoped instances visually.

decisions.decision: Generic saved views route through openGenericViewTab, query-based through openViewTab
decisions.choice: my_views.html uses two code paths: generic saved views (no query or query-scoped) call `openGenericViewTab(renderer, scopeQuery)`, while query-based promoted views keep `openViewTab()`. Unpin uses `deleteSavedView()` for generic and `demoteView()` for query-based.
decisions.rationale: Generic saved views need the new multi-instance tab system with scope binding. Query-based promoted views already work through the existing openViewTab() path. Separate delete methods because generic views may have no associated query_id — `demote_query()` requires one. Two-path pattern keeps backward compatibility while enabling the new feature.

decisions.decision: Kanban status field detection implementation — SHACL sh:in scan vs hardcoded field
decisions.choice: Implemented general SHACL sh:in PropertyShape scan in _detect_status_field(), preferring properties with "status" in path (case-insensitive), falling back to first property with non-empty in_values. Evolved beyond D286 which planned hardcoding to bpkm:taskStatus.
decisions.rationale: The SHACL-based approach is only marginally more complex than hardcoding (~30 lines vs ~10 lines) but automatically supports any Mental Model type that declares sh:in enum constraints on a property. The preference for "status" in the path name provides sensible defaults while the fallback ensures broader compatibility. Unit tests cover all edge cases.
decisions.revisable: No — strictly better than the hardcoded approach

decisions.decision: SPARQL _VOCAB_PREFIXES strategy — broad urn:sempkm: exclusion vs specific sub-namespace allow-list
decisions.choice: Explicit allow-list of ~28 specific internal urn:sempkm: sub-namespaces (query, user, workflow, etc.) that should NOT be enriched as data objects. urn:sempkm:model: is intentionally excluded so model ontology IRIs get enriched and rendered as vocab pills.
decisions.rationale: The broad "urn:sempkm:" entry caused ALL model ontology IRIs to be treated as internal/vocabulary, preventing pill rendering. An allow-list means new model ontology IRIs automatically get pill treatment. Only new internal machinery namespaces require list updates.

decisions.decision: Graph popover rendering — document.body with position:fixed vs z-index within container
decisions.choice: Append graph popovers to document.body with position:fixed and z-index:9999, using getBoundingClientRect() for viewport-relative positioning. Cleanup removes popovers from body on graph destroy.
decisions.rationale: .graph-container creates a stacking context via position:relative. Elevating z-index within that context cannot escape dockview chrome. Appending to document.body fully escapes all stacking contexts. Cleanup in registerCleanup prevents orphaned DOM nodes.

decisions.decision: Full-height view layout — shared .view-flex-column flex wrapper vs per-view calc()
decisions.choice: Shared .view-flex-column CSS class (display:flex; flex-direction:column; height:100%). Expandable children use flex:1; min-height:0. Used by both graph and kanban views.
decisions.rationale: Per-view calc() (e.g., calc(100% - 90px)) is fragile — breaks when toolbar height changes. Flex column delegates height distribution to the browser. Shared class keeps CSS DRY for future views. Table/cards use natural scrolling and don't need the wrapper.

decisions.decision: Dashboard block layout storage — keep SQLite JSON, not RDF
decisions.choice: DashboardSpec.blocks_json stays as SQLAlchemy JSON column. No migration to RDF named graphs.
decisions.rationale: Existing system has 968 lines across 4 backend modules, 1,076 lines of tests, proven GridStack serialization. Dashboard definitions are per-user config data, not knowledge graph entities. RDF migration would be significant effort with no clear benefit.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if dashboards need to be shared as linked data

decisions.decision: Widget config schema — keep Python type hints, defer JSON Schema (BLK-06)
decisions.choice: BlockTypeSpec.config_schema stays as dict[str, type] validated via isinstance(). JSON Schema formalization deferred.
decisions.rationale: Python type hints are simpler, work for all planned block types (flat config dicts), and the validation code is already well-tested with 30+ registry tests. JSON Schema adds value only for external plugin systems — not needed now.
decisions.revisable: Yes — if a plugin system needs machine-readable schemas

decisions.decision: M033 slice ordering — all six slices are independent, no inter-slice dependencies
decisions.choice: S01: Deployment (medium, data-integrity risk), S02: Isometric graph + icon toggle (high, CSS 3D + Cytoscape), S03: Calendar (low), S04: Map (low), S05: Federated SPARQL console (low), S06: App catalog (low). Each slice touches a different subsystem so no slice depends on another.
decisions.rationale: Deployment eliminates dangerous example.org default. Isometric graph is highest technical uncertainty (Cytoscape issue #1756). Calendar/map follow established view renderer pattern. Federation backend already exists — only console UI is new. App catalog is least coupled. Independence means slices can be reordered or dropped without affecting others.

decisions.decision: M033 requirement ID prefixes
decisions.choice: DEPLOY-01..04 for deployment, CAL-01..03 for calendar, MAP-01..03 for map, ISO-01..02 for isometric, ICON-01 for graph icons, FED-01..03 for federation, CAT-01..02 for app catalog. 18 requirements total.
decisions.rationale: Follows established provider-specific prefix convention (D209, D214, etc.). Each feature area gets its own prefix for clear traceability.

decisions.decision: Research correction — SPARQL console has zero federation UI code
decisions.choice: Research claimed console JS has detectServiceEndpoints(), fetchMirrorAllowlist(), handleMirrorClick(), and isEndpointAllowed(). Verified by rg: sparql-console.js (1666 lines) contains no 'mirror', 'SERVICE', 'federation', or 'allowlist' references. Backend mirror service/router exist (410 lines). All federation console UI must be built from scratch in S05.
decisions.rationale: Grep confirmed zero matches for federation-related terms in frontend/static/js/sparql-console.js and all files under frontend/static/js/. This adjusts S05 scope upward from "polish" to "build console integration".

decisions.decision: Isometric 2.5D approach — CSS 3D transform on Cytoscape container with inverse coordinate correction
decisions.choice: Apply rotateX(60deg) + rotateZ(-45deg) to Cytoscape container. Intercept mouse events and apply inverse transform matrix (~20 lines of matrix math) to correct coordinate mismatch. Fall back to parallax depth simulation (node size + opacity variation) if coordinate correction is unreliable across browsers.
decisions.rationale: Reuses all existing Cytoscape infrastructure (layouts, styling, popovers). Option B (z-position hack) isn't real isometric. Option C (custom renderer) is too much scope. The coordinate correction is well-documented in Cytoscape issue #1756 community workarounds. Ship as a layout option, not a separate renderer.
decisions.revisable: Yes — fall back to parallax if CSS 3D correction is unreliable

decisions.decision: Calendar view is read-only display — no inline drag-to-reschedule
decisions.choice: Calendar v1 renders events on the grid. Clicking opens the object tab for editing. No FullCalendar eventDrop/eventResize handlers for inline date modification.
decisions.rationale: Inline reschedule requires a write-back path for date property changes, which means a SPARQL UPDATE from the frontend or a new API endpoint. This exceeds v1 scope and adds complexity. Users can click through to the object editor to change dates.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add inline reschedule if users request it

decisions.decision: Map view ships functional with empty-state UX — no geo property bootstrapping
decisions.choice: No existing Mental Model types define lat/long coordinates. The map renderer ships complete but shows an instructive empty state explaining which RDF properties to add. No model changes to force-fit geo data.
decisions.rationale: The map view is a capability investment. Forcing geo properties into bpkm:Event (which has a string location field) would be artificial. Future models (Research Workflow, CRM with meeting locations) can add `wgs84:lat`/`wgs84:long` and the view works immediately.
decisions.revisable: Yes — add geo-enabled model types in a future milestone

decisions.decision: FullCalendar interaction approach — enable editable/selectable/droppable on existing CDN bundle
decisions.choice: Enable `editable:true`, `selectable:true`, `droppable:true` on the existing FullCalendar 6.1.17 CDN bundle (interaction plugin already included). `eventDrop`/`eventResize` call `object.patch` with `scheduledStart`/`scheduledEnd`. `select` handler opens new task form with pre-filled times. No separate interaction plugin script needed.
decisions.rationale: Research confirmed the standard FullCalendar CDN bundle includes `@fullcalendar/interaction`. M033 template already lazy-loads FullCalendar with CDN polling. Write-back uses existing `object.patch` command endpoint. D301 deferred inline reschedule — M034 delivers it.

decisions.decision: Frappe Gantt (MIT, zero deps, ~50KB SVG) for timeline/Gantt renderer
decisions.choice: Vendor Frappe Gantt as the timeline renderer. Integrates as the 8th generic view renderer (alongside table, card, graph, kanban, calendar, map, isometric). SVG-based with built-in dependency arrows, drag-to-reschedule, resize, and zoom levels.
decisions.rationale: vis-timeline has heavier deps and more complex API. FullCalendar Premium timeline costs $480 and is not MIT. Frappe Gantt is purpose-built for task timelines, MIT licensed, zero runtime deps, and has the exact feature set needed (bars, arrows, drag, zoom). Custom SVG would duplicate what Frappe Gantt already provides.
decisions.revisable: Yes — switch to custom SVG if Frappe Gantt proves inflexible

decisions.decision: Task scheduling properties — bpkm:scheduledStart/scheduledEnd/estimatedDuration complementing ppv:doDate
decisions.choice: Add `bpkm:scheduledStart` (xsd:dateTime), `bpkm:scheduledEnd` (xsd:dateTime), `bpkm:estimatedDuration` (xsd:string, ISO 8601 duration) to TaskShape. These complement `bpkm:dueDate` (when it's due) and `ppv:doDate` (which day to do it, date-only).
decisions.rationale: dueDate = deadline, doDate = day-level intent, scheduledStart/End = hour-level time block. All three are useful at different granularities. Calendar needs dateTime precision for time-grid placement. Duration enables block sizing independent of explicit end time. Additive change only — no existing properties modified, basic-pkm version bumps to 2.2.0.

decisions.decision: python-dateutil for backend RRULE expansion
decisions.choice: Add `python-dateutil~=2.9.0` to backend dependencies for `rrule.rrulestr()` to expand recurrence rules into virtual calendar events at query time.
decisions.rationale: Event model already has `bpkm:recurrenceRule` (xsd:string, RFC 5545 RRULE format) from calendar sync apps. python-dateutil is the standard Python library for RRULE parsing. Virtual expansion at query time (not stored objects) follows the Google Calendar pattern and avoids phantom object pollution in the triplestore.

decisions.decision: Cross-panel drag protocol — text/x-sempkm-iri dataTransfer type with IRI + title + duration
decisions.choice: Kanban and explorer drag handlers set `dataTransfer.setData('text/x-sempkm-iri', JSON.stringify({iri, title, duration}))` alongside existing `text/plain` (backward compat). Calendar's FullCalendar `drop` handler reads this to create a scheduled task at the drop time.
decisions.rationale: Extends the proven kanban drag pattern (currently uses `text/plain` with bare IRI). JSON payload carries title and estimated duration for immediate calendar block rendering before the server roundtrip. FullCalendar's `externalDrop` event provides the date/time from the drop target. `stopPropagation()` prevents dockview interference (proven in kanban M031 and canvas M008).

decisions.decision: M034 requirement ID prefixes — PLAN-01..PLAN-10
decisions.choice: Requirements PLAN-01 (time-blocking) through PLAN-10 (timeline scoping). 10 requirements total covering scheduling, calendar interaction, timeline, recurring tasks, templates, workflows, and composability.
decisions.rationale: New PLAN- prefix for the planning domain. Follows established prefix convention (D209, D285, D298).

decisions.decision: Frappe Gantt loaded from CDN, not vendored
decisions.choice: CDN-loaded from jsdelivr (`frappe-gantt@1.2.2` UMD bundle + CSS), not vendored in `frontend/static/vendor/`. Follows exact lazy-load IIFE pattern used by FullCalendar, Leaflet, Cytoscape, and Chart.js. Refines D304 which said "vendor".
decisions.rationale: The codebase consistently uses CDN loading for all external visualization libraries. Vendoring would diverge from the established pattern. Pinned to @1.2.2 for reproducibility.
decisions.revisable: Yes — can vendor if CDN availability becomes a concern

decisions.decision: RDF import: store imported triples directly with original IRIs, no IRI reminting
decisions.choice: Imported RDF subjects keep their original IRIs. No reminting to SemPKM `{namespace}/{Type}/{slug}` pattern. EventStore accepts arbitrary IRIs.
decisions.rationale: RDF import users expect their IRIs to be preserved. The object view queries `<iri> ?p ?o` and renders any IRI. Reminting would lose external linkability and violate user expectations for RDF data.

decisions.decision: RDF import: direct triple insertion without edge reification
decisions.choice: All parsed triples go into `urn:sempkm:current` as-is. URIRef-to-URIRef triples (e.g., `ex:alice schema:knows ex:bob`) are stored as direct triples, not reified as `sempkm:Edge` resources.
decisions.rationale: Reification is lossy and complex — some URIRef objects are vocabulary terms, not importable subjects. Edge detection is ambiguous without a heuristic. Direct triples are valid RDF, queryable via SPARQL, and preserve data fidelity. Edge Inspector won't show these — acceptable for v1.

decisions.decision: RDF import: one Operation per subject, commit_bulk for batches
decisions.choice: Group parsed triples by subject. Each subject becomes one Operation with operation_type="rdf.import". Use commit_bulk() for ≤1000 subjects, chunk into batches of 500 for larger imports.
decisions.rationale: Per-subject Operations provide fine-grained provenance. commit_bulk keeps event overhead low (~10 summary triples vs N*5). Direct Operation construction preserves original RDF data faithfully — imported data already has IRIs and typed literals.

decisions.decision: RDF import module: separate `/browser/rdf-import` router, not nested under Obsidian's `/browser/import`
decisions.choice: New `backend/app/rdf_import/` module with router prefix `/browser/rdf-import`.
decisions.rationale: The Obsidian router at `/browser/import` has `/{import_id}/...` path patterns. A nested `/browser/import/rdf` path could collide with import_id route matching. Separate prefix follows the Notion pattern (separate module at `/browser/notion`).

decisions.decision: Where to place M034 feature documentation in the user guide
decisions.choice: Extend existing chapters: Calendar/Timeline/Map views go in chapter 7 (Browsing and Visualizing), Task Templates and Review Workflows go in chapter 28 (Dashboards and Workflows).
decisions.rationale: Calendar, Timeline, and Map are renderers — they belong in the renderers chapter (7) alongside Table, Cards, Graph, and Kanban. Task Templates and Review Workflows are planning tools built on the workflow system — they belong with existing workflow docs in chapter 28. Preserves existing chapter structure without creating thin standalone chapters. Alternative (dedicated "Planning & Time-Blocking" chapter) rejected because it would scatter renderer documentation across two chapters.

decisions.decision: Orphan chapter renumbering strategy — sequential from 39 onward
decisions.choice: Rename 9 orphan files to chapters 39–47 (after current highest linked chapter 38). No renumbering of existing linked chapters.
decisions.rationale: Avoids touching any existing chapter numbers, which would break cross-references. Orphans get the next available numbers. Mental Model Catalog (currently duplicating 29) moves to 39, preserving its content as-is. Sync apps cluster together (41–44, 47) for logical grouping.

decisions.decision: Model packaging for business planning frameworks
decisions.choice: Single `business-planning` model archive with namespace `urn:sempkm:model:bp:`, containing all framework types in one installable package
decisions.rationale: Single model is simpler to install and enables cross-framework SPARQL queries without cross-model graph concerns. PPV model (11 types, 2186 lines) provides precedent for large models. All frameworks share base types (QuadrantItem, FrameworkSection) in a single namespace.
decisions.revisable: Yes — split into strategic-frameworks + operational-tools if single archive exceeds ~5000 lines

decisions.decision: Custom renderer dispatch — extend elif pattern, don't refactor registry
decisions.choice: Add new renderer type strings (`quadrant`, `bmc`, `okr`, `decision-matrix`) to `_VALID_RENDERERS` set and add elif branches in `generic_view()`. Don't refactor the dead `register_renderer()` into a real dispatch system.
decisions.rationale: The elif pattern is ugly but proven across 7 renderers, each with unique data fetching and template context needs. Refactoring to registry-based dispatch is a large tangent that doesn't deliver user value. The 4 new renderers can follow the exact same pattern. Wire the registry in a future cleanup milestone.
decisions.revisable: Yes — refactor to registry dispatch when renderer count exceeds 15

decisions.decision: Generic quadrant renderer parameterized by axis labels
decisions.choice: One `quadrant_view.html` template + `quadrant.js` + `quadrant.css` used by 6+ frameworks (Eisenhower, SWOT, BCG, Ansoff, Stakeholder Map, Risk Matrix). Axis labels, colors, and quadrant names passed as template context from the ViewSpec's SPARQL query and config.
decisions.rationale: Building 6 separate renderers for the same 2×2 layout would be massive duplication. The only difference is axis labels and quadrant names. A single parameterized renderer with config from the ViewSpec keeps CSS/JS DRY. Each framework's ViewSpec declares `quadrant` renderer with framework-specific config.

decisions.decision: M036 requirement ID prefix — BIZ-01 through BIZ-10
decisions.choice: Requirements BIZ-01 (model archive) through BIZ-10 (documentation). 10 requirements covering model install, 4 custom renderers, extended frameworks, cross-model edges, SPARQL queryability, E2E tests, and docs.
decisions.rationale: New BIZ- prefix for the business planning domain. Follows established prefix convention (D209, D285, D298, D308).

decisions.decision: Computed fields (OKR progress, Decision Matrix scores) via server-side Python in data endpoints
decisions.choice: OKR progress percentage = (current_value / target_value) × 100. Decision Matrix weighted score = Σ(weight × score). Computed in the Python data endpoint before template rendering. Not SHACL-AF rules, not client-side JS.
decisions.rationale: SHACL-AF computation would make values SPARQL-queryable (ideal) but adds significant rule complexity and requires inference re-run on every edit. Client-side JS loses SPARQL queryability. Server-side computation is the pragmatic middle: computed values are available in the rendered view and can be cached or materialized later.
decisions.revisable: Yes — migrate to SHACL-AF inference rules for SPARQL queryability when AI copilot needs it

decisions.decision: New `POST /api/copilot/chat` endpoint with dual-auth, separate from settings LLM proxy
decisions.choice: The copilot needs server-side system prompt injection (schema context, persona prompt, conversation history) before proxying to the LLM. The existing `llm_chat_stream` in settings.py is a simple passthrough. New endpoint uses `get_current_user_or_api` dual-auth and handles conversation persistence, context injection, and SPARQL generation internally. Settings proxy remains for raw LLM access.
decisions.rationale: Copilot logic (schema injection, self-correction, conversation history) shouldn't pollute the generic LLM proxy. Separation of concerns.

decisions.decision: SQLite per-message rows for conversation persistence — `copilot_conversations` + `copilot_messages` tables via Alembic
decisions.choice: Conversations are user state, not knowledge graph data — triplestore would pollute the RDF model. sessionStorage loses history on reload. Per-message rows (vs JSON blob) enable pagination, search, and per-conversation deletion. Follows persona module pattern (SQLAlchemy + Alembic + CRUD service).
decisions.rationale: SQLite is the right balance: persistent, queryable, schema-migrated. One row per message allows future conversation search and message-level linking.

decisions.decision: Separate `ai_personas` table from workspace `personas` — same CRUD pattern, different schema
decisions.choice: Workspace personas (M012) store dockview layout state. AI personas store system prompt templates, model preference, temperature. Different data, different purpose. Separate tables with same service pattern keep models clean.
decisions.rationale: Sharing a table would require nullable columns for both use cases and type discrimination. persona/ module is the pattern reference, not the storage target.

decisions.decision: SPARQL self-correction: max 2 retries (3 total), error message fed back to LLM
decisions.choice: LLMs frequently generate plausible but wrong SPARQL. 2 retries balances quality improvement vs latency. Error feedback includes parse error + available schema predicates. After 3 failures, show error and suggest rephrasing.
decisions.rationale: Well-documented pattern for LLM code generation. 3 attempts catches syntax and predicate errors. More indicates fundamental misunderstanding.

decisions.decision: M035 requirement IDs: AI-01 through AI-10
decisions.choice: 10 requirements covering copilot chat UI, SPARQL generation, query approval, graph context injection, conversation persistence, AI personas, object creation from chat, and 3-tier test harness (mock/Ollama/cloud).
decisions.rationale: New AI- prefix for the AI copilot domain. Follows established prefix convention (D209, D285, D298, D308, D319).

decisions.decision: Character-based token estimation (~4 chars/token), no tiktoken dependency
decisions.choice: tiktoken requires ~3MB data download and is OpenAI-specific. Character estimation is within 10-15% for English, sufficient for soft context budgets. Configurable default 4000 tokens for graph context.
decisions.rationale: Avoids heavy dependency for approximate arithmetic. Budget is a soft limit — precision not needed. Works across all LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama/Llama).
decisions.revisable: Yes — add tiktoken if token-precise budgeting becomes necessary

decisions.decision: Copilot chat endpoint — new POST /api/copilot/chat SSE with dedicated CopilotService
decisions.choice: New endpoint with server-side system prompt injection (schema context), SPARQL detection in streamed content, and query approval via POST /api/copilot/approve. Separate from existing /browser/settings/llm/chat/stream and /api/llm/stream. ai_router from M028 wired into main.py alongside new copilot_router.
decisions.rationale: Copilot needs schema context injection, SPARQL detection, and approval state — none supported by existing LLM proxies. Dedicated service class keeps copilot logic isolated from extension AI endpoints.

decisions.decision: SPARQL predicate validation — non-blocking warnings for unknown predicates, blocking rejection for mutation keywords
decisions.choice: Unknown predicates (not in installed model SHACL shapes) log a warning but do not reject the query. Mutation keywords (INSERT, DELETE, DROP, CLEAR, LOAD, CREATE, COPY, MOVE, ADD) are strict rejections. Mutation check is regex-based — catches keywords in string literals too (known limitation, low risk).
decisions.rationale: SHACL shape coverage is incomplete — rdf:type, rdfs:label, and other common predicates aren't declared in shapes. Blocking on unknowns would false-negative on legitimate queries. Mutation blocking is strict because the copilot should never modify the graph.
decisions.revisable: Yes — tighten predicate validation as shape coverage improves

decisions.decision: SSE client uses ReadableStream reader instead of EventSource API
decisions.choice: Frontend copilot.js parses SSE manually from a fetch() ReadableStream rather than using the browser's EventSource API.
decisions.rationale: EventSource only supports GET requests. The copilot chat endpoint requires POST with a JSON body (messages array, model selection). ReadableStream gives full control over request method, headers, and body while parsing the same SSE wire format.

decisions.decision: CopilotService lives in `backend/app/copilot/` module, not `backend/app/services/`
decisions.choice: CopilotService, schemas, and __init__.py placed in a dedicated `backend/app/copilot/` package rather than as a single file in the services directory.
decisions.rationale: The copilot module has its own Pydantic schemas, will gain conversation persistence and persona integration in S02/S03 — a package structure accommodates growth. Follows the same pattern as `backend/app/commands/`, `backend/app/sparql/`, `backend/app/auth/`.

decisions.decision: Graph context serialization: human-readable grouped text with labels, not raw RDF triples
decisions.choice: serialize_context() resolves IRIs to labels, compacts predicates, groups by relationship type, outputs natural language text (e.g. "Project 'Q1 Planning' has tasks: 'Review Goals'").
decisions.rationale: LLMs process natural language far better than RDF syntax. Raw triples waste token budget on angle brackets and full IRIs. Matches the schema context pattern from S01's build_schema_context().

decisions.decision: Conversation persistence: per-message rows in copilot_messages table, not JSON blob
decisions.choice: Each message stored as a separate row with FK to copilot_conversations, not as a JSON blob column on the conversation.
decisions.rationale: Per-message rows enable pagination, cross-conversation search, and per-message metadata (SPARQL query attachment, approval status). Matches the SparqlQueryHistory per-record pattern. JSON blob requires full deserialization for any operation.

decisions.decision: Separate 2000-token budget for graph context, independent of 4000-token schema context budget
decisions.choice: Graph context gets its own DEFAULT_GRAPH_TOKEN_BUDGET = 2000 (~8000 chars), separate from schema context's DEFAULT_TOKEN_BUDGET = 4000.
decisions.rationale: Schema context (type structure) and graph context (instance data) vary independently — installing more models shouldn't shrink instance context space. Combined total ~6000 tokens (24KB) stays well within LLM context limits.

decisions.decision: 3-tier LLM test strategy: mock (CI), Ollama (local), cloud (budget-capped)
decisions.choice: Mock server for CI determinism (<5s), Ollama compose for local real inference, cloud tier with CostTracker budget cap ($1.00 default). Tier auto-selected via env vars in getLlmTier().
decisions.rationale: Mock gives deterministic assertions for CI. Ollama gives real inference without API costs. Cloud gives production-realistic testing with budget guardrails. Each tier has a dedicated compose file or configuration path.

decisions.decision: Mock LLM server pattern matching priority: claims first for backward compat
decisions.choice: _select_response() checks routes in order: claims > SPARQL > create-object > summarize > generic. Claims route stays first because M028 browser extension tests depend on it.
decisions.rationale: Adding copilot routes to the existing mock server must not break M028 claim detection tests. Priority ordering with keyword matching ensures backward compatibility while supporting the new copilot flows.

decisions.decision: Context data in SQLite `user_context` table — single-row-per-user upsert, not RDF
decisions.choice: Context is ephemeral state (current location, activity, time period), not knowledge. Single-row upsert keeps exactly one current-state record per user. TTL-based staleness via `updated_at`. No history.
decisions.rationale: Triplestore is for knowledge graph data. Context is transient device state that changes every few minutes. SQLite is the right home for ephemeral per-user state.

decisions.decision: Expo managed workflow with development builds for mobile app
decisions.choice: `expo-location` provides `startGeofencingAsync` + `TaskManager.defineTask` for background geofencing. `expo-notifications` for unified push. `expo-calendar` for calendar read. Development builds support all native modules. JS/TS ecosystem aligns with existing project.
decisions.rationale: Flutter rejected (Dart, no ecosystem overlap). Bare React Native rejected (Expo wraps the hard native parts). Expo Go rejected (doesn't support native modules).
decisions.revisable: Yes — if Expo geofencing proves unreliable, consider react-native-background-geolocation (paid)

decisions.decision: Direct FCM via `firebase-admin` Python SDK for push notifications
decisions.choice: Mobile app uses `getDevicePushTokenAsync()` for native FCM/APNs token. Backend dispatches via `firebase-admin` `messaging.send()`.
decisions.rationale: Aligns with self-hosted philosophy — no dependency on Expo's push servers. firebase-admin is Google's official SDK.
decisions.revisable: Yes — can switch to Expo Push Service if direct FCM setup proves too complex

decisions.decision: `ContextBroadcast` SSE fan-out — same pattern as `LintBroadcast`
decisions.choice: New class with asyncio.Queue subscribers, publish-to-all, full-queue client eviction. Context-specific event types: context_update, persona_switched, context_stale.
decisions.rationale: LintBroadcast is proven. No need for shared base class — the two broadcasts serve different event streams. Extract base if a third broadcast is needed.

decisions.decision: CTX-01 through CTX-19 requirement IDs for user context domain
decisions.choice: 19 requirements covering context API, SSE streaming, rules engine, mobile app, geofencing, calendar, activity, push notifications, and settings UI.
decisions.rationale: New CTX- prefix follows established convention (D209, D285, D298, D308, D319, D325).

decisions.decision: Rules evaluate on context update POST, not on a timer
decisions.choice: ContextService.update() calls RulesEngine.evaluate() synchronously after persisting. Separate TTL checker on timer for staleness only.
decisions.rationale: Context updates are naturally event-driven (geofence transitions, calendar boundaries). Polling wastes CPU.

decisions.decision: Manual persona switch suppresses auto-switching until next context change
decisions.choice: Override flag on user_context row. Cleared on next context update POST.
decisions.rationale: Users expect manual choice to stick. "Until next context change" is a natural reset — the next geofence transition signals a meaningful state change.
decisions.revisable: Yes — could add configurable lock duration

decisions.decision: Context rule conditions: JSON dict with AND semantics, first-match-wins by priority
decisions.choice: Conditions are field-name→value equality pairs — all must match. Rules sorted by priority DESC, first match wins. No OR logic or complex expressions.
decisions.rationale: Covers stated use case (location + time → persona) with minimal complexity. JSON conditions are schema-free and extensible. Priority ordering gives users predictable control. OR/complex expressions deferred.
decisions.revisable: Yes — can evolve JSON structure to support OR logic later

decisions.decision: Rule evaluation runs synchronously in context update request handler, not as broadcast subscriber
decisions.choice: RulesEngine.evaluate() called directly in update_context() after broadcast.publish(). Not decoupled via broadcast subscription.
decisions.rationale: Synchronous evaluation is simpler, avoids subscriber lifecycle management, and rule evaluation is fast (one DB query + in-memory matching). Decoupling adds complexity without benefit at this scale.
decisions.revisable: Yes — extract to subscriber if evaluation becomes expensive

decisions.decision: Geofence sync failures in mobile app are non-blocking — zone CRUD succeeds even if registerGeofences() fails
decisions.choice: Log geofence registration failures as warnings (zones.geofence_sync_failed), show no user-facing error. Zone data is persisted server-side regardless.
decisions.rationale: Geofence registration is an OS-level operation that can fail for many reasons (permissions revoked, region limit exceeded, background restrictions). Blocking zone CRUD on geofence registration would make the UI feel broken when the backend is healthy. The zone data is the source of truth; geofences are re-registered on next app launch or zone mutation.
decisions.revisable: Yes — could add user-visible retry button if geofence sync failures are common

decisions.decision: Schedule rules in StateClient (JSON), media items + daily plans in RDF
decisions.choice: Rules are ephemeral app configuration stored via StateClient key-value. MediaItem, DailyMediaPlan stored as RDF objects via CommandClient.
decisions.rationale: Rules change frequently and don't benefit from graph querying. Media items are knowledge artifacts queryable by SPARQL ("what did I listen to this week?") and linkable to other objects. Consistent with M037 context rules pattern (SQLite config, not RDF).
decisions.revisable: Yes — could move rules to RDF if rule reasoning becomes valuable

decisions.decision: Podcast polling reuses feedparser + conditional GET from RSS Reader (M010), not a new dependency
decisions.choice: Feed polling in media-scheduler app reuses the same feedparser library and conditional GET pattern (ETag/Last-Modified) from apps/rss-reader/services/feed_service.py. No shared library extraction — code is duplicated into the media-scheduler app.
decisions.rationale: feedparser is already a project dependency. The RSS Reader's feed_service.py is a proven pattern (subscribe, fetch, parse, dedup). Extracting a shared library adds coupling between two apps that should be independently deployable. Duplication is cheaper than abstraction at this point.
decisions.revisable: Yes — could extract shared feed-polling library if a third app needs it

decisions.decision: External API clients use raw httpx (via SDK HttpClient), no Python SDK wrappers
decisions.choice: YouTube Data API v3 and Spotify Web API accessed via direct HTTP requests through the App SDK's HttpClient, not via google-api-python-client or spotipy.
decisions.rationale: Consistent with all existing sync apps (Linear, GitHub, Jira, Monday, Google Calendar) which use raw HTTP. Avoids new dependencies, keeps the API surface explicit, and the SDK's HttpClient enforces domain allowlists.
decisions.revisable: Yes — could adopt SDK wrappers if API complexity grows

decisions.decision: Context-driven plan adaptation uses 2-minute debounce on context SSE events
decisions.choice: Media scheduler subscribes to GET /api/context/stream SSE. Context changes trigger rule re-evaluation after a 2-minute debounce window. Immediate re-evaluation only for geofence transitions (location_zone changes).
decisions.rationale: Prevents thrashing from rapid activity detection changes (walking↔stationary during a meeting). Location zone changes are discrete events (geofence transitions) that warrant immediate response. Activity/calendar changes are noisy and benefit from settling time.
decisions.revisable: Yes — debounce duration configurable via app settings

decisions.decision: Media playback via deep links to native apps, not embedded players
decisions.choice: For v1, all media types open via deep links: Spotify URI (spotify:track:...), YouTube URL, podcast app URL scheme. No embedded web player or audio player in the SemPKM mobile app.
decisions.rationale: Building a reliable audio/video player is out of scope. Users already have preferred apps for each media type. Deep links provide the best UX — one tap to start playing in the right app. Podcast audio player could be added later as a progressive enhancement.
decisions.revisable: Yes — could add HTML5 audio player for podcasts in future slice

decisions.decision: Media scheduler ontology: flat enum (sh:in) for sourceType, not OWL subclasses
decisions.choice: Namespace `urn:sempkm:model:media-scheduler:` with prefix `ms:`. Three types: MediaSource, MediaItem, MediaCategory. sourceType uses sh:in ["podcast","youtube","spotify"].
decisions.rationale: Flat enum simplifies SPARQL (single type, filter by sourceType) vs subclass hierarchy (PodcastSource, YouTubeSource, SpotifySource). Consistent with other model patterns in the codebase.

decisions.decision: Media scheduler app owns its model (media-scheduler), does not extend rss-feeds
decisions.choice: MediaItem ≠ Article (different semantics: playback status vs read/starred, duration, enclosure). MediaSource ≠ FeedSubscription (sourceType discriminator). Code pattern reused, not the RDF types.
decisions.rationale: Independent evolution of both models. No confusing type overlap. Consistent with app-per-model separation.

decisions.decision: Spotify OAuth requires HTTPS redirect URI — HTTP rejected
decisions.choice: The Spotify developer portal enforces HTTPS on redirect URIs. User confirmed this during setup. S04 must plan for HTTPS callback routing.
decisions.rationale: Discovered by user during Spotify portal configuration. Unlike some OAuth providers, Spotify does not allow HTTP even for localhost development.

decisions.decision: Time range rule evaluation behavior when current_time is missing from context
decisions.choice: Fail-closed — rule does not match. If the system can't determine the current time, a time-scoped rule should not fire.
decisions.rationale: A time-scoped rule matching when there's no time data could trigger media playback at inappropriate times. Fail-closed is the safe default for context-driven automation. Wildcard behavior is already available via null conditions for fields where "match any" is intentional.

decisions.decision: How to handle old daily plan entries when regenerating a plan
decisions.choice: Patch old entries to entryStatus="replaced" via object.patch. No object.delete.
decisions.rationale: object.delete is a separate permission the app may not have. Patching status preserves history (what was planned before regeneration) and is consistent with the event-sourced write model. The today view SPARQL excludes "replaced" entries.

decisions.decision: Object-level ownership model (F-002)
decisions.choice: Document shared-data model only. Multi-tenant isolation is not a goal — sharing is handled via federation and shared named graphs.
decisions.rationale: Single-user/small-team is the target. Federation provides cross-instance sharing. Per-object ownership would touch every CRUD endpoint for a use case that doesn't exist.

decisions.decision: Session management hardening (F-013)
decisions.choice: All three: wire revoke_all_sessions() to Settings UI, cap concurrent sessions at 10 per user, add daily background cleanup task.
decisions.rationale: revoke_all_sessions() already exists but is unwired. Session cap prevents unbounded accumulation. Daily cleanup replaces startup-only cleanup for long-running instances.

decisions.decision: Demo mode safeguard (F-019)
decisions.choice: Startup warning log when DEMO_MODE=true and APP_BASE_URL is non-localhost. No hard block.
decisions.rationale: Demo mode is intentional for the hosted demo. A warning surfaces misconfiguration without blocking legitimate use. Hard block adds override-flag complexity for an unlikely scenario.

decisions.decision: Central SPARQL query builder approach for injection prevention
decisions.choice: Build a custom SPARQLBuilder in backend/app/sparql/builder.py using rdflib's URIRef.n3() and Literal.n3() for safe serialization. Provides iri(), literal(), values_clause(), triple_pattern(), and where_block() methods. Not a full query DSL — a parameterized string builder that guarantees safe interpolation of IRIs and literals into SPARQL templates. No external library — the Python SPARQL ecosystem has no mature parameterized query builder for remote endpoints.
decisions.rationale: Research findings: (1) SPARQLWrapper has no parameterized query support (open issue since 2018). (2) Apache Jena's ParameterizedSparqlString is Java-only with known limitations. (3) rdflib's prepareQuery/initBindings doesn't work with remote SPARQLStore endpoints. (4) The pudo/sparqlquery project is abandoned. (5) rdflib's .n3() method IS the right primitive — URIRef.n3() rejects malicious IRIs with exceptions, Literal.n3() properly escapes all injection characters. Building on .n3() gives us type-safe serialization without a new dependency. The builder consolidates 9 scattered escape functions + _validate_iri into one authoritative module.

decisions.decision: Whether to standardize htmx patterns: 14 trigger types, inconsistent debounce (200ms vs 300ms), revealed vs intersect, and undocumented conventions
decisions.choice: Document conventions (innerHTML default, 300ms standard debounce, custom event naming pattern). Fix the 200ms debounce outlier to 300ms. Migrate revealed triggers to intersect once. No heavy refactoring.
decisions.rationale: htmx patterns are already 88% consistent — formalizing the de facto standard prevents drift. The 200ms vs 300ms debounce difference is likely accidental (same intent, different author). revealed is a legacy htmx trigger; intersect once is the documented modern equivalent.

decisions.decision: SPARQL injection defense strategy — validate early at HTTP boundary
decisions.choice: Call safe_iri() at HTTP parameter extraction point (router layer), not deep in service call chains. Return 400 with warning-level security log on invalid IRIs. Defense-in-depth: safe_iri() also called on system-derived IRIs in service layer.
decisions.rationale: If safe_iri() is only called deep in the service layer, ValueError propagates as 500 instead of 400. Early validation at the router gives clean error responses and security audit logging. The service-layer calls catch edge cases where system data becomes corrupted or an internal caller bypasses the router.

decisions.decision: CORS header ownership — single source of truth
decisions.choice: FastAPI CORSMiddleware is the sole CORS authority. All CORS add_header directives removed from nginx.conf and nginx.demo.conf. Caddy passes through without adding CORS. A dedicated _WellKnownCORSMiddleware overrides CORSMiddleware specifically for /.well-known/sempkm to always return Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (browser extension discovery must work from any origin).
decisions.rationale: Dual CORS headers (nginx + FastAPI) caused duplicate header issues and confusion about which layer controlled access. Single-sourcing in FastAPI makes CORS testable via unit tests and keeps proxy layers as pure pass-through. The well-known override uses BaseHTTPMiddleware with `del response.headers[key]` (not .pop() — Starlette MutableHeaders doesn't implement pop).

decisions.decision: HTTP security headers standard set for all proxy layers
decisions.choice: 6 security headers added to nginx.conf, nginx.demo.conf, and Caddyfile.cloud: X-Content-Type-Options (nosniff), X-Frame-Options (DENY), Referrer-Policy (strict-origin-when-cross-origin), Permissions-Policy (camera=(),microphone=(),geolocation=()), Content-Security-Policy (self + CDN allowlist), server_tokens off. CSP allows scripts/styles from unpkg.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net, cdnjs.cloudflare.com plus 'unsafe-inline' for existing inline scripts.
decisions.rationale: F-021 finding. Headers applied at proxy layer (nginx/Caddy) so they cover all responses including static files, not just FastAPI routes. CSP allowlist matches the three CDNs used by FullCalendar, Leaflet, and Yasgui — would be removed when those are vendored (M029 pipeline). 'unsafe-inline' is required for existing htmx inline event handlers and inline styles.
decisions.revisable: Yes — tighten CSP when CDN deps are vendored and inline scripts are eliminated

decisions.decision: Obsidian vault upload size cap
decisions.choice: Obsidian upload location capped at 500m via client_max_body_size. Default nginx locations remain at 10m.
decisions.rationale: F-027 finding — the Obsidian import endpoint had client_max_body_size 0 (unlimited), allowing unbounded uploads. 500MB accommodates large Obsidian vaults while preventing abuse. Other endpoints stay at nginx default 10m.

decisions.decision: M043/S03 — Single-use magic link enforcement location
decisions.choice: Single-use check in AuthService (DB layer) rather than tokens.py. The stateless itsdangerous signature verification in tokens.py stays pure — the stateful DB check (UsedMagicToken hash lookup + insert) lives in AuthService.check_and_consume_magic_token(). Router calls both in sequence: signature first, then single-use check.
decisions.rationale: Preserves clean separation between cryptographic verification (stateless, no DB) and stateful consumption tracking. The itsdangerous verify is fast and rejects most invalid tokens before hitting the DB.

decisions.decision: M043/S03 — API token scope enforcement surface
decisions.choice: Scope enforcement applied to API-surface endpoints (SPARQL, commands, copilot) that accept Bearer tokens. Browser-only endpoints (htmx objects, admin) left on cookie-only auth — scope checks not added since sessions inherit full role permissions.
decisions.rationale: The practical external API surface is SPARQL + commands + copilot. Object mutations via external clients go through the commands router (already scoped). Admin endpoints are owner-gated browser-only. Adding scope checks to htmx endpoints would require changing their auth dependency chain for no security benefit — those endpoints don't accept Bearer tokens.

decisions.decision: M043/S03 — Periodic session/token cleanup scheduling mechanism
decisions.choice: asyncio.create_task with sleep loop in lifespan, cancelled on shutdown. No APScheduler or BackgroundTasks dependency.
decisions.rationale: Zero new dependencies. Proper cancellation via task.cancel() in lifespan shutdown. The cleanup is lightweight (two DELETE queries) and runs once daily — doesn't justify a scheduler library.

decisions.decision: Audit logging failure isolation policy
decisions.choice: log_security_event() catches all exceptions internally — audit logging never fails the parent operation
decisions.rationale: Security audit logging is observability infrastructure. If the audit log DB is temporarily unavailable, the login/token-creation/session-revocation operation must still succeed. The helper manages its own DB session and swallows exceptions with ERROR-level logging.

decisions.decision: Centralized fetch wrapper design: apiFetch() behavior and migration strategy
decisions.choice: window.apiFetch() wraps native fetch, returns raw Response on success, throws structured error ({status, body, response}) on non-2xx, catches AbortError silently (returns undefined), supports {silent:true} to suppress toasts, redirects to /login.html on 401. All 167 callers migrated with {silent:true} since each file has its own error UX. One intentional exemption: auth.js /api/auth/me uses raw fetch (needs ?next= on 401 redirect). Toast CSS moved from workspace.css to theme.css for cross-page availability.
decisions.rationale: Every file already has its own error handling (inline UI messages, custom toasts, status elements). Double-toasting from apiFetch + caller would confuse users. Using {silent:true} universally means apiFetch provides the safety net (network errors, unexpected 5xx) while callers keep their specific UX. Auth.js /api/auth/me is exempt because apiFetch's 401 redirect loses the ?next= query parameter needed for return-URL preservation. Toast CSS must be in theme.css (not workspace.css) so it renders on auth pages that don't load the workspace stylesheet.

decisions.decision: Window namespace consolidation strategy for cross-IIFE globals
decisions.choice: All custom globals migrate from `window.X` to `window.SemPKM.X`. Namespace object initialized at top of api-fetch.js (earliest custom script in load order). Three-phase rollout: T01 adds exports + backward-compat shims to JS files, T02 migrates templates to use SemPKM.X, T03 removes shims. Existing `window.SemPKMSettings`/`SemPKMLayouts`/`SemPKMCanvas` left as-is (already namespaced by concatenated naming). Internal names like `_sempkmGraph` keep the `_sempkm` prefix under the namespace (mechanical safety over cosmetic cleanup). Debug/admin pages using app.js local functions excluded from migration.
decisions.rationale: Three-phase rollout with shims ensures zero breakage at any intermediate stage — templates and E2E tests work against both old and new names during migration. Keeping existing `SemPKM*` concatenated names avoids unnecessary churn for already-safe globals. Keeping `_sempkm` prefixes under the namespace object is mechanically safer than renaming (shim pattern works identically for all globals). Debug pages have their own local `switchTab`/`executeCommand` from `app.js` — migrating those would break them since `app.js` is not an IIFE and doesn't export to window.SemPKM.
decisions.revisable: Yes — the `_sempkm` prefix redundancy under SemPKM namespace could be cleaned up in a follow-up cosmetic rename

decisions.decision: How to handle decorative per-section colors in BMC, quadrant, OKR, and decision-matrix CSS files
decisions.choice: Full conversion: add ~15 primitive tokens (--_color-bmc-*, reuse existing --_color-*-500 for quadrant) to theme.css with dark-mode overrides, then convert all decorative rgba() to color-mix(in srgb, var(--_color-X) PCT%, transparent). No exemptions for these files — the ≤20 rgba budget applies globally.
decisions.rationale: The research initially suggested leaving BMC/quadrant/OKR decorative colors as exemptions (counting toward ≤20 rgba). However, those files alone have 127 standalone rgba values — far exceeding the budget. Full conversion with primitive tokens adds ~15 lines to theme.css but enables proper dark-mode support (brighter section colors on dark backgrounds) and eliminates ~291 lines of dark-mode override blocks across these files. The quadrant colors already match existing primitives (--_color-green-500 etc.), reducing new tokens needed.
decisions.revisable: No — tokens are the right approach for dark-mode correctness

decisions.decision: Federation SHA-256 hash verification backward compatibility strategy (F-036)
decisions.choice: Federation hash verification is backward-compatible: always include content_hash in exports, verify when present in imports, log warning when absent. Never reject hashless patches — existing peers don't send hashes.
decisions.rationale: Breaking federation by rejecting hashless patches would require coordinated upgrades across all federation peers. Warning-only for missing hashes allows gradual rollout. Mandatory verification when present catches tampering from upgraded peers.
